title.en: Volume 384 Biographies 143: Chen Kangbo, Liang Kejia, Wang Che, Ye Yiwen, Jiang Fei, Ye Yong, Ye Heng
title.raw: 卷三百八十四 列傳第一百四十三 陳康伯 梁克家 汪澈 葉義問 蔣芾 葉顒 葉衡 Volume 384 Biographies 143: Chen Kangbo, Liang Kejia, Wang Che, Ye Yiwen, Jiang Fei, Ye Yong, Ye Heng

sentences.zh: 陳康伯

translations.literal: Chen Kangbo
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kangbo

sentences.zh: 陳康伯，字長卿，信之弋陽人。

translations.literal: Chen Kangbo, styled Changqing, was a native of Yiyang in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Chen Kangbo, courtesy name Changqing, was a native of Yiyang in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父亨仲，提舉江東常平。

translations.literal: His father Hengzhong was Director of Ever-Normal Granaries for Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: His father Hengzhong served as Director of Ever-Normal Granaries for Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 康伯幼有學行。

translations.literal: From youth Kangbo had learning and conduct.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Kangbo was noted for his scholarship and personal integrity.

sentences.zh: 宣和三年，中上舍丙科。

translations.literal: In the third year of Xuanhe, he passed the upper dormitory division C examination.
translations.idiomatic: In 1121, he passed the upper dormitory division C examination at the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 累遷太學正。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Director of the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 丁內艱。

translations.literal: He mourned his father's death.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning upon his father's death.

sentences.zh: 貴溪盜將及其鄉，康伯起義丁逆擊，俘其渠魁，邑得全。

translations.literal: When bandits from Guixi were about to reach his home district, Kangbo raised volunteer militia and counterattacked, capturing their ringleader, and the district was preserved intact.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits from Guixi approached his home district, Kangbo raised local militia and counterattacked, capturing the ringleaders and saving the district from ruin.

sentences.zh: 建炎末，為敕令刪定官，預修《紹興敕令》。

translations.literal: At the end of the Jianyan era, he served as an official revising imperial codes, and took part in compiling the Shaoxing Imperial Codes.
translations.idiomatic: Near the end of the Jianyan era, he served as a code-revision official and helped compile the Shaoxing Imperial Codes.

sentences.zh: 尋通判衢州，攝郡事。

translations.literal: Soon he became Vice Prefect of Quzhou and administered prefectural affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Prefect of Quzhou, where he also administered prefectural affairs in the prefect's stead.

sentences.zh: 盜發白馬原，康伯督州兵濟王師進討，克之。

translations.literal: When bandits rose at Baima Plain, Kangbo directed the prefectural troops to assist the imperial army in advancing against them, and they took it.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose at Baima Plain, Kangbo directed prefectural troops to support the imperial army in a punitive campaign and captured them.

sentences.zh: 除太常博士，改提舉江東常平茶鹽。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then reassigned as Commissioner of Ever-Normal Granaries, Tea, and Salt for Jiangdong.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, then reassigned to supervise ever-normal granaries, tea, and salt in Jiangdong.

sentences.zh: 高宗進蹕建康，康伯以職事過闕，得對，因請擇將，上開納。

translations.literal: When Emperor Gaozong proceeded to Jiankang, Kangbo passed through the capital on official business, was granted an audience, and thereupon requested that commanders be chosen; the emperor received this openly.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong moved his court to Jiankang, Kangbo happened to be in the capital on official business and was granted an audience, where he urged the emperor to select capable generals. The emperor received the suggestion favorably.

sentences.zh: 紹興八年，除樞密院大計議官。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Shaoxing, he was appointed Grand Deliberator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In 1138, he was appointed Grand Deliberator of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 累遷戶部司勳郎中。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Bureau Section Director in the Ministries of Revenue and of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to serve concurrently as Bureau Section Director in the Ministries of Revenue and of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 康伯與秦檜太學有舊，檜當國，康伯在郎省五年，泊然無求，不偷合。

translations.literal: Kangbo had known Qin Hui from the Imperial Academy. When Qin held state power, Kangbo spent five years in the ministry offices, tranquil and without seeking advancement, not currying favor in secret.
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo had known Qin Hui from their days at the Imperial Academy. When Qin dominated the government, Kangbo spent five years in the ministry offices without ambition or scheming, refusing to ingratiate himself.

sentences.zh: 十三年，始遷軍器監。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year, he was at last transferred to the Directorate of Armaments.
translations.idiomatic: Not until the thirteenth year of Shaoxing was he transferred to the Directorate of Armaments.

sentences.zh: 借吏部尚書使金，至汴將晡，不供餉，閉戶臥勿問；

translations.literal: He was temporarily appointed Minister of Personnel and sent as envoy to Jin. When he reached Bian near evening, no provisions were supplied. He shut his door and lay down, making no inquiry.
translations.idiomatic: Appointed acting Minister of Personnel and sent as envoy to Jin, he reached Bian near dusk without being offered provisions. He shut his door and went to bed without a word of complaint.

sentences.zh: 入夜，館人扣戶謝不敏，亦不對。

translations.literal: After nightfall the host knocked at his door to apologize for his shortcomings, but Kangbo did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: That night the host knocked on his door to apologize for the lapse, but Kangbo offered no response.

sentences.zh: 後因金使至，詔康伯館伴，端午賜扇帕，與論拜受禮，言者以生事論，罷知泉州。

translations.literal: Later, when a Jin envoy arrived, Kangbo was ordered by edict to serve as his host. At the Dragon Boat Festival the court bestowed fans and silk; he discussed the ritual of bowing to receive them, and critics accused him of picking quarrels, so he was dismissed and appointed prefect of Quanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Later, when a Jin envoy arrived, the court ordered Kangbo to serve as host envoy. When fans and silk were bestowed at the Dragon Boat Festival, he discussed the ritual of bowing to receive them. Critics charged him with stirring up trouble, and he was removed from office and sent to govern Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 海盜間作，朝廷遣劉寶、成閔逐捕，康伯以上意招懷，盜多出降，籍為兵。

translations.literal: Sea pirates arose intermittently. The court dispatched Liu Bao and Cheng Min to pursue and capture them. Kangbo, in accord with the emperor's intent, sought to win them over by kindness, and many pirates surrendered and were registered as soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: Sea pirates emerged intermittently, and the court dispatched Liu Bao and Cheng Min to hunt them down. Acting on the emperor's policy of clemency, Kangbo persuaded many to surrender, and they were enrolled as soldiers.

sentences.zh: 久之，不逞者陰倡亂，康伯訊得實，論殺之，州以無事。

translations.literal: After some time, malcontents secretly incited rebellion. Kangbo investigated and established the facts, condemned them to death, and the prefecture remained untroubled.
translations.idiomatic: After a time, discontented elements secretly stirred up rebellion. Kangbo investigated, confirmed the plot, had the ringleaders executed, and the prefecture was kept at peace.

sentences.zh: 秩滿，三奉祠，垂十年。

translations.literal: When his term ended, he three times received temple sinecures, for nearly ten years.
translations.idiomatic: When his term expired, he held temple sinecures on three separate occasions, for nearly ten years in all.

sentences.zh: 檜死，起知漢州，將出峽，召對，除吏部侍郎。

translations.literal: When Qin died, Kangbo was recalled to govern Hanzhou. As he was about to leave the gorges, he was summoned for an audience and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin's death, Kangbo was recalled to govern Han Prefecture. Before he had even left the Three Gorges, he was summoned for an audience and appointed Vice Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 康伯首請節用寬民，凡州縣取民無藝，許監司互察，臺諫彈劾。

translations.literal: Kangbo was the first to request thrift in expenditure and relief for the people. Whenever prefectures and counties extorted from the people without limit, supervisory commissioners were permitted to inspect one another, and censorial officials were to impeach offenders.
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo was the first to call for frugal government and relief for the people. Wherever local officials extorted the people without restraint, he proposed that supervisory commissioners be empowered to investigate one another and that censorial officials impeach offenders.

sentences.zh: 尋兼禮、戶部。

translations.literal: Soon he also served concurrently in the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon given concurrent charge of the Ministries of Rites and Revenue.

sentences.zh: 乞約歲用，會所入，儲什之一二備水旱。

translations.literal: He requested that annual expenditure be budgeted against revenue, with one or two tenths set aside against flood and drought.
translations.idiomatic: He proposed setting annual expenditure against projected revenue and reserving one or two tenths as a buffer against flood and drought.

sentences.zh: 奏上，議竟不決。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted, but deliberation ended without a decision.
translations.idiomatic: His memorial reached the throne, but deliberations ended without a decision.

sentences.zh: 兼刑部。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently in the Ministry of Justice.
translations.idiomatic: He was given additional charge of the Ministry of Justice.

sentences.zh: 前此有司希檜意興大獄，康伯平讞直冤，士大夫存歿多賴之。

translations.literal: Before this, officials had sought to please Qin by launching major prosecutions. Kangbo balanced verdicts and rectified wrongful convictions, and many officials, living and dead, owed their salvation to him.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qin, officials had launched major prosecutions to win favor. Kangbo rebalanced verdicts and cleared wrongful convictions, and many officials owed their lives or posthumous vindication to him.

sentences.zh: 除吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 宰臣擬用「權尚書」出命，高宗顧曰：「朕且大用，何權為？

translations.literal: The chief councillors proposed issuing the appointment as "Acting Minister," but Gaozong turned and said: "I am about to employ him fully — why 'acting'?"
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillors proposed issuing the appointment as "Acting Minister," but Gaozong turned and said, "I intend to use him in full measure — why call him acting?"

sentences.zh: 」尋拜參知政事。

translations.literal: Soon he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 自孫道夫使北還，已聞金以買馬非約為言，朝廷特恃和，康伯與同知樞密院事王倫白發其端，倫使還，乃言和好無他，康伯持初論不變。

translations.literal: Ever since Sun Daofu returned from his mission to the north, it had been heard that the Jin complained that purchasing horses was not part of the treaty. The court relied solely on peace. Kangbo and Wang Lun, Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, were the first to bring up the matter. When Lun returned from his mission, he said the alliance remained sound and there was nothing else to it, but Kangbo held to his original view unchanged.
translations.idiomatic: Ever since Sun Daofu's return from the north, the court had heard that Jin was complaining that horse purchases fell outside the treaty terms. The court still clung to the hope of peace. Kangbo and Wang Lun, Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, were the first to raise the alarm. When Wang returned from his own mission, he insisted the alliance was intact, but Kangbo never wavered from his initial judgment.

sentences.zh: 九月，以通奉大夫守尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事，例賜銀絹，康伯固辭，減半，又辭。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, as Grand Master for Court Audience, he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State and Concurrent Grand Councillor. By precedent silver and silk were bestowed; Kangbo firmly declined, and when the amount was halved he declined again.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Ministry of State and Concurrent Grand Councillor with the rank of Grand Master for Court Audience. By precedent he was offered silver and silk; he firmly declined, and when the gift was halved he declined again.

sentences.zh: 兼史院。

translations.literal: He also served concurrently in the History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He was also given charge of the History Institute.

sentences.zh: 上嘗謂其「靜重明敏，一語不妄發，真宰相也。

translations.literal: The emperor once said of him: "Calm, grave, clear, and quick — not a word spoken rashly — a true chief minister."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once described him as "calm, deliberate, and sharp — never speaking rashly — a true chief minister."

sentences.zh: 」又命與湯思退輔政，事勿憚商論，惟其當而已。

translations.literal: He was also ordered to assist in governance with Tang Situi. In affairs they were not to shrink from discussion; only what was right mattered.
translations.idiomatic: He was also ordered to govern alongside Tang Situi, with instructions to debate freely and decide matters on merit alone.

sentences.zh: 康伯言：「大臣事當盡公，若依阿植黨，此鄙夫患失者，臣非惟不敢，亦素不能。

translations.literal: Kangbo said: "The business of a grand minister should be fully public. To fawn and favor and form factions — that is the conduct of a petty man who fears loss. Your servant not only dares not do so — I have never been capable of it."
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo said, "A chief minister's duty is to serve the public good. To fawn, build factions, and cling to office is the way of a petty man. I not only dare not do such things — I have never been capable of them."

sentences.zh: 」高宗歎其長者。

translations.literal: Gaozong sighed that he was a man of mature character.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong praised him as a man of mature and upright character.

sentences.zh: 普安郡王居潛藩，高宗一日謂康伯，當以使相封真王，今宜冠以屬籍，於是詔以為皇子，封建王，實三十年二月也。

translations.literal: The Prince of Pu'an resided in the concealed palace. One day Gaozong told Kangbo that he should be enfeoffed as a true prince with the rank of commissioner-grandee, and should now be entered in the imperial clan register. Thereupon an edict named him imperial son and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jian. This was in fact the second month of the thirtieth year.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Pu'an still lived in the inner palace as heir apparent in waiting. One day Gaozong told Kangbo that he ought to be enfeoffed as a full prince under the commissioner-grandee rank and entered in the imperial clan register. An edict then declared him imperial son and enfeoffed him as Prince of Jian — this was in the second month of 1160.

sentences.zh: 明年三月，拜光祿大夫、尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: In the third month of the following year, he was appointed Grand Master of Splendor and Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of the following year he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State with the rank of Grand Master of Splendor.

sentences.zh: 五月，金遣使賀天申節，出嫚言，求淮、漢地，指取將相大臣，且以淵聖凶問至。

translations.literal: In the fifth month, Jin sent envoys to congratulate the Heavenly Progenitor Festival. They uttered insults, demanded the Huai and Han territories, singled out generals, ministers, and grand councillors, and also brought word of the death of Emperor Qinzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth month Jin sent envoys to congratulate the Heavenly Progenitor Festival. They spoke contemptuously, demanded the territories between the Huai and Han rivers, named specific generals and ministers for extradition, and also brought news of Emperor Qinzong's death.

sentences.zh: 康伯主禮部侍郎黃中之論，持斬衰三年。

translations.literal: Kangbo upheld the argument of Vice Minister of Rites Huang Zhong and observed three years of unhemmed mourning.
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo sided with Vice Minister of Rites Huang Zhong and insisted on three years of mourning in the most severe grade.

sentences.zh: 先是，葉義問、賀允中使還，言金必敗盟，康伯請早為之備，建四策：一，增劉錡荊南軍，以重上流；

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ye Yiwen and He Yunzhong returned from their missions, they reported that Jin would surely break the alliance. Kangbo requested early preparations and proposed four measures: first, increase Liu Qi's Jingnan army to strengthen the upper Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ye Yiwen and He Yunzhong returned from their missions, they reported that Jin would surely renounce the treaty. Kangbo urged early preparations and proposed four measures: first, reinforce Liu Qi's army in Jingnan to strengthen the upper Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 二，分畫兩淮地，命諸將結民社，各保其境；

translations.literal: Second, demarcate the Two Huai region and order the generals to organize local communities so each could defend his territory.
translations.idiomatic: Second, demarcate the Two Huai region and order local generals to organize militia communities so each area could defend itself.

sentences.zh: 三，劉寶獨當淮東，將驕卒少，不可倚；

translations.literal: Third, Liu Bao alone held the Huai east — the generals were arrogant and the troops few; he could not be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: Third, Liu Bao alone held eastern Huai; his officers were arrogant and his troops too few to be trusted.

sentences.zh: 四，沿江諸郡修城積糧，以固內地。

translations.literal: Fourth, the Yangtze river counties should repair walls and store grain to fortify the interior.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, the counties along the Yangtze should repair city walls and stockpile grain to secure the interior.

sentences.zh: 至是，召三衙帥及楊存中至都堂議舉兵，又請侍從、臺諫集議，康伯傳上旨曰：「今日更不問和與守，直問戰當如何。

translations.literal: At this point, the commanders of the Three Palace Commands and Yang Cunzhong were summoned to the chief councillors' hall to discuss raising troops. He also requested that attendants and censorial officials meet for deliberation. Kangbo relayed the emperor's intent: "Today let us no longer ask about peace or defense — ask directly how war should be waged."
translations.idiomatic: At this juncture the commanders of the Three Palace Commands and Yang Cunzhong were summoned to the chief councillors' hall to discuss mobilization. Kangbo also called for a joint consultation of attendants and censorial officials, relaying the emperor's charge: "Today let us set aside debate over peace or mere defense — I want to know how we should fight."

sentences.zh: 」時上意雅欲視師，內侍省都知張去為陰沮用兵，且陳退避策，中外妄傳幸閩、蜀，人情洶洶。

translations.literal: At this time the emperor himself wished to review the armies. Zhang Quwei, Chief Director of the Inner Service, secretly discouraged the use of force and also proposed a strategy of retreat. Inside and outside the court, false rumors spread that the emperor would flee to Min or Shu, and public feeling was in turmoil.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor himself wished to take personal command of the armies, but Zhang Quwei, Chief Director of the Inner Service, secretly discouraged war and urged retreat. Rumors spread that the court would flee to Fujian or Sichuan, and public panic mounted.

sentences.zh: 右相朱倬無一語，同知樞密院事周麟之受命聘金，憚不欲行，康伯獨以為己任，奏曰：「金敵敗盟，天人共憤，今日之事有進無退，聖意堅決，則將士之意自倍。

translations.literal: The Right Grand Councillor Zhu Zhuo said not a word. Zhou Linzhi, Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, had been ordered to go on a mission to Jin but feared going and wished not to. Kangbo alone took it as his own responsibility and memorialized: "The Jin enemy has broken the alliance — heaven and men alike are enraged. In today's business there is advance but no retreat. If Your Majesty's resolve is firm, the spirit of officers and soldiers will be doubled of itself."
translations.idiomatic: Right Grand Councillor Zhu Zhuo offered not a word. Zhou Linzhi, Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs, had been ordered to serve as envoy to Jin but feared to go. Kangbo alone accepted the burden as his own and memorialized: "Jin has broken the treaty — heaven and men alike are enraged. Today there is no retreat, only advance. If Your Majesty's resolve is firm, the troops' morale will redouble of itself."

sentences.zh: 願分三衙禁旅助襄、漢，待其先發應之。

translations.literal: I wish to divide the Palace Commands' capital garrison to assist Xiang and Han, and wait for the enemy to move first, then respond.
translations.idiomatic: I ask that the Three Palace Commands' capital garrison be dispatched to reinforce Xiangyang and the Han River region, to respond once the enemy moves first.

sentences.zh: 」康伯勉周麟之以國事，麟之語侵康伯，康伯曰：「使某不為宰相，當自行，大臣與國存亡，雖死安避。

translations.literal: Kangbo urged Zhou Linzhi in the name of state affairs. Linzhi's words insulted Kangbo. Kangbo said: "If I were not chief minister, I would go myself. A grand minister shares life and death with the state — even unto death, how could one evade it?"
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo pressed Zhou Linzhi on the grounds of national duty. Zhou responded with insults, to which Kangbo replied, "Had I not been chief minister, I would have gone myself. A grand minister shares the fate of the state — even death is no excuse for shirking."

sentences.zh: 」麟之竟以辭行罷，尋貶責。

translations.literal: Linzhi ultimately declined on grounds of illness and was dismissed; soon he was demoted and censured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhou ultimately pleaded illness to avoid going and was dismissed; he was soon demoted and censured.

sentences.zh: 殿中侍御史陳俊卿言當用張浚，且乞斬張去為以作士氣。

translations.literal: Palace Remonstrance Official Chen Junqing said Zhang Jun should be employed, and also requested the execution of Zhang Quwei to rally military spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance Official Chen Junqing argued that Zhang Jun should be put in command, and called for Zhang Quwei's execution to rally troop morale.

sentences.zh: 康伯以俊卿振職，奏權兵部侍郎。

translations.literal: Kangbo, because Junqing had fulfilled his duty vigorously, memorialized to appoint him acting Vice Minister of War.
translations.idiomatic: Impressed by Chen Junqing's forceful discharge of duty, Kangbo recommended him for appointment as acting Vice Minister of War.

sentences.zh: 九月，金犯廬州，王權敗歸，中外震駭，朝臣有遣家豫避者。

translations.literal: In the ninth month, Jin attacked Luzhou. Wang Quan was defeated and retreated. Inside and outside the court all were shaken with alarm; some court officials sent their families ahead to escape in advance.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month Jin attacked Luzhou. Wang Quan's army was routed. Court and country alike were shaken; some officials sent their families away in advance.

sentences.zh: 康伯獨具舟迎家入浙，且下令臨安諸城門扃鐍率遲常時，人恃以安。

translations.literal: Kangbo alone prepared boats to bring his family into Zhe, and also ordered that the city gates of Lin'an be locked more slowly than usual; the people relied on this and felt secure.
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo alone prepared boats to bring his family into Zhejiang, and ordered that Lin'an's city gates be closed more slowly than usual — through this the people found reassurance.

sentences.zh: 敵迫江上，召楊存中至內殿議之，因命就康伯議。

translations.literal: As the enemy pressed the river, Yang Cunzhong was summoned to the inner palace for deliberation, and was then ordered to confer with Kangbo.
translations.idiomatic: As the enemy pressed toward the river, Yang Cunzhong was summoned to the inner palace for consultation and then sent to confer with Kangbo.

sentences.zh: 康伯延之入，解衣置酒，上聞之已自寬。

translations.literal: Kangbo invited him in, loosened his garments, and set out wine. When the emperor heard of it, he was already reassured of himself.
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo invited him in, loosened his garments, and offered wine. When the emperor heard of this, his own anxiety eased.

sentences.zh: 翌日，入奏曰：「聞有勸陛下幸越趨閩者，審爾，大事去矣，盍靜以待之。」

translations.literal: The next day he entered and memorialized: "I have heard that some urge Your Majesty to go to Yue and hasten to Min. If this be so, the great enterprise is lost. Would it not be better to wait calmly?"
translations.idiomatic: The next day he memorialized: "I hear that some urge Your Majesty to flee to Shaoxing and then on to Fujian. If that is true, all is lost. Better to remain calm and wait."

sentences.zh: 一日，忽降手詔：「如敵未退，散百官。

translations.literal: One day an imperial letter suddenly descended: "If the enemy does not retreat, disband the officials."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor suddenly issued a handwritten edict: "If the enemy does not withdraw, dismiss the entire bureaucracy."

sentences.zh: 」康伯焚之而後奏曰：「百官散，主勢孤矣。

translations.literal: Kangbo burned it and only then memorialized: "If the officials are dispersed, the ruler's position is isolated."
translations.idiomatic: Kangbo burned the edict, then memorialized: "If the officials are dismissed, Your Majesty stands alone."

sentences.zh: 」上意既堅，請下詔親征，以葉義問督江、淮軍，虞允文參謀軍事。

translations.literal: Once the emperor's resolve was firm, Kangbo requested an edict for a personal campaign. Ye Yiwen was to oversee the Jiang-Huai armies, and Yu Yunwen was to assist in military planning.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor's resolve was firm, Kangbo urged a proclamation of personal campaign. Ye Yiwen was appointed to oversee the Jiang-Huai armies, with Yu Yunwen as military strategist.

sentences.zh: 上初命朱倬為都督，倬辭，乃命義問。

translations.literal: The emperor at first appointed Zhu Zhuo as overall commander; Zhu declined, and Ye Yiwen was appointed instead.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor first named Zhu Zhuo supreme commander, but Zhu declined, and Ye Yiwen was appointed in his place.

sentences.zh: 允文尋敗敵于采石，金主亮為其臣下所斃而還。

translations.literal: Soon Yu defeated the enemy at Caishi. Jin Emperor Hailing was killed by his own officials and the Jin forces withdrew.
translations.idiomatic: Yu soon routed the enemy at Caishi. Emperor Hailing of Jin was assassinated by his own court, and the invading army withdrew.

sentences.zh: 方亮之犯江，國人即立葛王褒。

translations.literal: Just as Hailing was invading the Yangtze, the people of Jin immediately enthroned Prince Ge Wanyan Yong.
translations.idiomatic: While Hailing was still pushing south toward the Yangtze, the Jin court had already enthroned Prince Ge, Wanyan Yong.

sentences.zh: 三十二年，始遣高忠建來告登位，議授書禮，康伯以誼折之，於是報書始用敵國禮。

translations.literal: In the thirty-second year, Gao Zhongjian was first sent to announce the enthronement. When the ritual for receiving the letter was discussed, Kangbo overrode it on grounds of propriety, and thus the reply letter first used the ritual toward an enemy state.
translations.idiomatic: In 1162, Gao Zhongjian arrived to announce the new emperor's accession. When court ritual for receiving the letter was debated, Kangbo objected on grounds of propriety, and the court's reply was accordingly drafted in the forms reserved for an enemy state.

sentences.zh: 高宗倦勤，有與子意，康伯密贊大議，乞先正名，俾天下咸知聖意，遂草立太子詔以進。

translations.literal: Gaozong wearied of rule and intended to yield to his son. Kangbo secretly supported the great decision, requesting that the heir first be properly named so all under heaven might know the sage intent. He then drafted the edict establishing the crown prince and submitted it.
translations.idiomatic: Weary of rule, Gaozong wished to abdicate in favor of his son. Kangbo quietly supported the plan, urging that the heir's status be formally settled first so the realm would understand the emperor's intent. He then drafted the edict establishing the crown prince and submitted it for approval.

sentences.zh: 及行內禪禮，以康伯奉冊。

translations.literal: When the inner abdication rites were performed, Kangbo was ordered to present the ritual document.
translations.idiomatic: When the abdication ceremony was performed, Kangbo was charged with presenting the investiture document.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，命兼樞密使，進封信國公，禮遇殊渥，但呼丞相而不名。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong took the throne, Kangbo was ordered to serve concurrently as Commissioner of Military Affairs, was advanced to Duke of Xin, received exceptionally generous treatment, and was addressed only as Chief Minister without using his name.
translations.idiomatic: Upon Xiaozong's accession, Kangbo was made concurrent Commissioner of Military Affairs, advanced to Duke of Xin, and granted exceptional honors — the emperor addressed him only as "Chief Minister," never by name.

sentences.zh: 康伯自建康扈從回，即以病祈去位，不允。

translations.literal: When Kangbo returned from escorting the court from Jiankang, he immediately pleaded illness to leave office; this was not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On returning from Jiankang with the imperial procession, Kangbo at once pleaded illness and asked to retire; the emperor refused.

sentences.zh: 明年，改元隆興，請益堅，遂以太保、觀文殿大學士、福國公判信州。

translations.literal: The following year, when the reign era was changed to Longxing, his request grew firmer. Thereupon, as Grand Mentor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and Duke of Fu, he was assigned to govern Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, when the era name was changed to Longxing, his request grew more insistent. He was finally released as Grand Mentor, Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Literature, and Duke of Fu, assigned to govern Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 上慰勞甚勤，且曰：「有宣召，慎勿辭。

translations.literal: The emperor consoled and honored him with great care, and said: "If there is an imperial summons, take care not to decline."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor comforted him warmly and said, "If I summon you again, do not refuse."

sentences.zh: 」宰執即府餞別，百官班送都門外。

translations.literal: The chief councillors offered a farewell banquet at his residence, and officials in ranks escorted him beyond the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: The chief councillors held a farewell feast at his residence, and officials lined up to escort him beyond the capital gate.

sentences.zh: 已又辭郡，丐外祠，除醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: Later he again declined the prefecture and requested an outside temple sinecure; he was appointed Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: He soon resigned the prefectural post and requested an honorary temple appointment; he was made Commissioner of the Liquan Abbey.

sentences.zh: 二年八月，起判紹興府，且令赴闕奏事，復辭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the second year, he was recalled to govern Shaoxing Prefecture and ordered to come to court to report affairs; he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the second year he was recalled to govern Shaoxing Prefecture and ordered to report at court; he declined again.

sentences.zh: 未幾，召陪郊祀。

translations.literal: Before long he was summoned to attend the suburban sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: Before long he was summoned to attend the suburban sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 時北兵再犯淮甸，人情驚駭，皆望康伯復相。

translations.literal: At this time northern troops again invaded the Huai region; public feeling was alarmed, and all looked to Kangbo to become chief minister again.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops again invaded the Huai region, panic spread and everyone hoped Kangbo would return as chief minister.

sentences.zh: 上出手劄，遣使即家居召之。

translations.literal: The emperor issued a handwritten letter and dispatched an envoy to summon him directly from his home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent a personal letter and dispatched an envoy to summon him directly from his home.

sentences.zh: 未出里門，拜尚書左僕射、同中書平章事兼樞密使，進封魯國公。

translations.literal: Before he had left the village gate, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State, Concurrent Grand Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs, and advanced to Duke of Lu.
translations.idiomatic: Before he had even left his neighborhood, he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of State, Concurrent Grand Councillor and Commissioner of Military Affairs, and advanced to Duke of Lu.

sentences.zh: 親故謂康伯實病，宜辭，康伯曰：「不然。

translations.literal: Relatives and friends said Kangbo was truly ill and ought to decline. Kangbo said: "Not so."
translations.idiomatic: Relatives and friends urged that he was truly ill and should decline; Kangbo replied, "Not at all."

sentences.zh: 吾大臣也，今國家危，當輿疾就道，幸上哀而歸之爾。

translations.literal: I am a grand minister. Now the state is in peril; I ought to take to my carriage though ill and set out on the road, hoping only that the emperor in compassion will let me return.
translations.idiomatic: I am a chief minister. The state is in peril — I should travel even in sickness, trusting that the emperor in his mercy will release me when the crisis passes.

sentences.zh: 」道聞邊遽，兼程以進，至闕下，詔子安節、婿文好謙掖以見，減拜賜坐。

translations.literal: On the road he heard urgent news from the border and pressed forward day and night. When he reached the palace, an edict ordered his son Anjie and son-in-law Wen Haoqian to support him as he was presented, reducing the bows due him and granting him a seat.
translations.idiomatic: En route he heard urgent news from the frontier and traveled day and night. At court an edict allowed his son Anjie and son-in-law Wen Haoqian to support him during his audience; the usual bows were waived and he was granted a seat.

sentences.zh: 間日一會朝，許肩輿至殿門，仍給扶，非大事不署。

translations.literal: Every other day he attended court, was permitted to ride in a palanquin to the palace gate, was still provided with aides, and did not sign documents unless the matter was great.
translations.idiomatic: He attended court every other day, was permitted a palanquin to the palace gate, was provided with attendants, and signed documents only on major affairs.

sentences.zh: 敵師退，尋以目疾免朝謁，臥家，旬餘一奏事。

translations.literal: When the enemy army withdrew, he soon was exempted from court audience on account of eye disease, and remained at home, memorializing on affairs once every ten-odd days.
translations.idiomatic: After the enemy withdrew, he was soon excused from court audiences on account of eye trouble; he remained at home and reported on affairs roughly once every ten days.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年正月上辛，有事南郊，康伯起陪祠，已即丐歸，章屢上，不許。

translations.literal: On the upper xin day of the first month of the first year of Qiandao, when the southern suburban sacrifice was performed, Kangbo rose to attend the rite. Immediately afterward he requested to return home; memorial after memorial was submitted, but not granted.
translations.idiomatic: On the first upper-xin day of the first month of Qiandao (1165), when the southern suburban sacrifice was held, Kangbo attended despite his illness. Immediately afterward he petitioned to retire; repeated memorials were refused.

sentences.zh: 一日出殿門，喘劇，輿至第薨，年六十有九。

translations.literal: One day as he left the palace gate, his panting became severe. When the palanquin reached his residence, he died, aged sixty-nine sui.
translations.idiomatic: One day, leaving the palace gate, his breathing grew labored. He died at his residence in the palanquin, aged sixty-nine.

sentences.zh: 贈太師，諡「文恭」，擇日臨奠，子偉節固辭，乃止。

translations.literal: He was posthumously enfeoffed as Grand Preceptor and given the posthumous title "Reverent in Culture." A day was chosen for the emperor to attend the mourning rites in person, but his son Weijie firmly declined, and this was stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously enfeoffed Grand Preceptor with the temple name Wengong ("Reverent in Culture"). A day was set for the emperor to attend his funeral in person, but his son Weijie firmly declined, and the plan was dropped.

sentences.zh: 命工部侍郎何俌護喪歸。

translations.literal: He Bing, Vice Minister of Public Works, was ordered to escort the coffin home.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Minister of Public Works He Bing was ordered to escort the coffin home.

sentences.zh: 二子：偉節，除直秘閣；

translations.literal: Two sons: Weijie was appointed Directly to the Secret Archive;
translations.idiomatic: He had two sons: Weijie was appointed to the Secret Archive;

sentences.zh: 安節，賜同進士出身，五辭不受，上手劄批諭，寄留省中以成其美，康伯薨，給還之。

translations.literal: Anjie was granted the status of having passed the Presented Scholar examination with honors. He declined five times and did not accept. The emperor wrote a letter of instruction in his own hand and had it kept at the ministry to complete the honor. When Kangbo died, it was returned to him.
translations.idiomatic: Anjie was granted the status of a Presented Scholar by special decree; he declined five times. The emperor wrote in his own hand urging acceptance and had the decree held at the ministry to preserve the honor intact. After Kangbo's death it was returned to the family.

sentences.zh: 慶元初，配享孝宗廟庭，改諡「文正」。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qingyuan, he was paired in sacrifice at Xiaozong's temple, and his posthumous title was changed to "Upright in Culture."
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Qingyuan era he was enshrined in Xiaozong's temple, and his posthumous title was changed to Wenzheng ("Upright in Culture").

sentences.zh: 梁克家

translations.literal: Liang Kejia
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kejia

sentences.zh: 梁克家，字叔子，泉州晉江人。

translations.literal: Liang Kejia, styled Shuzi, was a native of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kejia, courtesy name Shuzi, was a native of Jinjiang in Quan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 幼聰敏絕人，書過目成誦。

translations.literal: From childhood he was surpassingly quick-witted; texts he read once he could recite.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood he was exceptionally quick-witted; whatever he read once he could recite from memory.

sentences.zh: 紹興三十年，廷試第一，授平江簽判。

translations.literal: In the thirtieth year of Shaoxing, he ranked first in the palace examination and was appointed Signing Administrator of Pingjiang.
translations.idiomatic: In 1160 he ranked first in the palace examination and was appointed Signing Administrator of Pingjiang.

sentences.zh: 時金主亮死，眾皆言可乘機進取，克家移書陳俊卿，謂：「敵雖退，吾兵力未振，不量力而動，將有後悔。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Hailing of Jin had died, and everyone said the moment could be seized for advance. Kejia wrote to Chen Junqing, saying: "Though the enemy has withdrawn, our military strength is not yet revived. To act without measuring our capacity will bring regret."
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Hailing of Jin had just died, everyone argued that the moment should be seized for an offensive. Kejia wrote to Chen Junqing, saying, "Though the enemy has withdrawn, our armies are not yet restored. To act without measuring our strength will bring regret."

sentences.zh: 」俊卿歸以白丞相陳康伯，歎其遠慮。

translations.literal: Junqing returned and reported this to Chief Minister Chen Kangbo, who sighed at his farsightedness.
translations.idiomatic: Junqing returned and reported this to Chief Minister Chen Kangbo, who praised his farsightedness.

sentences.zh: 召為秘書省正字，遷著作佐郎。

translations.literal: He was summoned as Corrector in the Secretariat and promoted to Assistant Compiler in the Institute for the Compilation of Historical Records.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as Corrector in the Secretariat and promoted to Assistant Compiler in the Institute for the Compilation of Historical Records.

sentences.zh: 時災異數見，克家奏宜下詔求言，從之，令侍從、臺諫、卿監、郎官、館職疏闕失。

translations.literal: At that time calamities and portents repeatedly appeared. Kejia memorialized that an edict should be issued inviting counsel. The emperor agreed and ordered attendant officials, censors and remonstrators, directors and supervisors, bureau officials, and academy scholars to submit memorials on deficiencies.
translations.idiomatic: Calamities and portents were appearing with increasing frequency. Kejia memorialized that the emperor should issue an edict inviting counsel. The request was granted, and attendant officials, censors, remonstrators, directors, supervisors, bureau officials, and academy scholars were ordered to submit memorials on governmental failings.

sentences.zh: 克家條六事：一正心術，二立紀綱，三救風俗，四謹威柄，五定廟算，六結人心。

translations.literal: Kejia listed six matters: first, rectifying the ruler's mind; second, establishing discipline; third, rescuing customs; fourth, guarding against abuse of power; fifth, fixing military strategy; sixth, binding hearts together.
translations.idiomatic: Kejia set forth six priorities: rectifying the ruler's mind, establishing institutional discipline, restoring social customs, guarding against abuse of power, settling military strategy, and winning the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 其論定廟算，謂今邊議不過三說，曰將、兵、財，語甚切直。

translations.literal: In his discussion of fixing military strategy, he said frontier debates came down to no more than three points — generals, troops, and finances — and his language was very pointed and direct.
translations.idiomatic: In his section on military strategy, he argued that frontier debates always came down to three things — commanders, troops, and finances — and his language was strikingly blunt.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: Through repeated promotions he became Drafting Official of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive appointments to Drafting Official of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 使金，金以中朝進士第一，敬待之，即館宴射，連數十發中的。

translations.literal: On a mission to Jin, Jin treated him with respect because he had ranked first among palace examination graduates of the Central Court. At a banquet in the hostel they had an archery contest, and he hit the target with dozens of consecutive shots.
translations.idiomatic: On a mission to Jin, he was received with respect as the top palace examination graduate of the Central Court. At a banquet in the guesthouse they held an archery contest, and he hit the target with dozens of shots in a row.

sentences.zh: 金人來賀慶會節，克家請令金使入朝由南門，百官由北門，從者毋輒至殿門外，以肅朝儀，詔定為令。

translations.literal: When Jin envoys came to congratulate on the Celebration Assembly Festival, Kejia requested that Jin envoys enter the court by the South Gate, that all officials use the North Gate, and that attendants not approach outside the palace gates at will, so as to solemnize court ceremony. An edict fixed this as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: When Jin envoys came to congratulate the court on the Celebration Assembly Festival, Kejia requested that they enter by the South Gate while officials used the North Gate, and that attendants not gather outside the palace gates, so as to preserve court decorum. An edict made this permanent regulation.

sentences.zh: 郊祀有雷震之變，克家復條六事。

translations.literal: During the suburban sacrifice there was a change of thunder and lightning. Kejia again listed six matters.
translations.idiomatic: During the suburban sacrifice thunder and lightning struck. Kejia again set forth his six-point program.

sentences.zh: 遷給事中，凡三年，遇事不可，必執奏無隱。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Supervising Secretary. In all three years, whenever he found something unacceptable, he invariably submitted a steadfast memorial without concealment.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to Supervising Secretary, he served three years in that post and, whenever he found a matter unacceptable, always submitted a forthright memorial without holding back.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏：「陛下欲用實才，不喜空言，空言固無益，然以空言為懲，則諫爭之路遂塞，願有以開導之。

translations.literal: He once memorialized: "Your Majesty wishes to employ men of real talent and does not care for empty talk. Empty talk is indeed of no use, yet if empty talk is made grounds for punishment, the path of remonstrance and debate will be blocked. I hope Your Majesty will provide some means to guide and encourage it."
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized: "Your Majesty wishes to employ men of real talent and dislikes empty talk. Empty talk is indeed useless, but if it becomes grounds for punishment, the path of remonstrance will be closed. I hope Your Majesty will find ways to encourage frank counsel."

sentences.zh: 」上欣納，因命條具風俗之弊，克家列四條，曰欺罔、苟且、循默、奔競，上手筆獎諭。

translations.literal: The emperor accepted this gladly and then ordered a detailed listing of the evils of custom. Kejia listed four items: deception, perfunctoriness, silent conformity, and scrambling for advancement. The emperor wrote with his own hand to commend and instruct him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor accepted this gladly and ordered a detailed account of prevailing social ills. Kejia listed four: deception, perfunctoriness, silent conformity, and ruthless careerism. The emperor wrote him a personal commendation.

sentences.zh: 乾道五年二月，拜端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: In the second month of the fifth year of Qiandao, he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Illuminating Governance and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of 1169, he was appointed Academician of the Hall for Illuminating Governance and Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，參知政事。

translations.literal: The next year he became Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 又明年，兼知院事。

translations.literal: The year after that he also concurrently directed the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The year after that he also took charge of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 初修金好，金索所獲俘，啟釁未已。

translations.literal: When relations with Jin were first renewed, Jin demanded the captives they had taken, and provocations did not cease.
translations.idiomatic: When relations with Jin were first restored, Jin demanded the captives they had taken, and provocations continued without end.

sentences.zh: 克家請築楚州城，環舟師于外，邊賴以安。

translations.literal: Kejia requested that the walls of Chuzhou be built and naval forces stationed around it, and the frontier relied on this for security.
translations.idiomatic: Kejia requested that Chuzhou's walls be rebuilt and naval forces stationed around it, and the frontier owed its security to this measure.

sentences.zh: 在政府，與虞允文可否相濟，不苟同。

translations.literal: In the government he and Yu Yunwen supported or checked each other and did not agree perfunctorily.
translations.idiomatic: In office he and Yu Yunwen balanced and checked each other and never agreed merely for the sake of agreement.

sentences.zh: 皇太子初立，克家請選置官屬，增講讀員，遂以王十朋、陳良翰為詹事，中外稱得人。

translations.literal: When the Crown Prince was first established, Kejia requested the selection and appointment of staff and an increase in lecturers and readers. Wang Shipeng and Chen Lianghan were then appointed Grand Mentors of the Heir Apparent, and within and without the court all praised the appointments as fitting men.
translations.idiomatic: When the Crown Prince was first installed, Kejia requested the selection of staff and an increase in lecturers and readers. Wang Shipeng and Chen Lianghan were appointed Grand Mentors of the Heir Apparent, and court and country alike praised the appointments as excellent choices.

sentences.zh: 允文主恢復，朝臣多迎合，克家密諫，數不合，力丐去。

translations.literal: Yunwen advocated recovery of lost territory, and many court officials followed suit. Kejia remonstrated in secret, often disagreeing, and strenuously begged to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Yunwen advocated recovering lost territory, and many court officials fell in with him. Kejia remonstrated in private, often disagreeing, and repeatedly begged to resign.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「兵終不可用乎？

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Are troops finally unusable?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "So war is finally out of the question?"

sentences.zh: 」克家奏：「用兵以財用為先，今用度不足，何以集事？

translations.literal: Kejia memorialized: "In employing troops, finances come first. Today expenditures are insufficient — how can tasks be accomplished?"
translations.idiomatic: Kejia replied, "War depends first on finances. With revenues insufficient today, how can any campaign be mounted?"

sentences.zh: 」上改容曰：「朕將思之。

translations.literal: The emperor changed expression and said: "I will think on this."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's expression changed. "I will consider it," he said.

sentences.zh: 」詰朝，上面諭曰：「朕終夜思卿言，至當，毋庸去。」

translations.literal: The next morning the emperor addressed him in person, saying: "I thought on your words all night — they are entirely right. Do not leave."
translations.idiomatic: The next morning the emperor addressed him in person: "I thought on your words all night — they are entirely right. Do not resign."

sentences.zh: 八年，詔更定僕射為左右丞相，拜克家為右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: In the eighth year an edict redesignated the Left and Right Grand Counsellors as Left and Right Grand Chancellors, and Kejia was appointed Right Grand Chancellor and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict redesignated the Left and Right Grand Counsellors as Left and Right Grand Chancellors, and Kejia was appointed Right Grand Chancellor and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 一日，上謂宰執曰：「近過德壽宮，太上頤養愈勝，天顏悅懌，朕退不勝喜。

translations.literal: One day the emperor told the chief ministers: "I recently passed by Deshou Palace. The Retired Emperor's nourishing of life grows ever better, his countenance cheerful and content. When I withdrew I could not contain my joy."
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor told his chief ministers, "I recently visited Deshou Palace. The Retired Emperor's health and spirits are better than ever, his face bright with contentment. I could hardly contain my joy on leaving."

sentences.zh: 」克家奏：「堯未得舜以為己憂，既得舜，固宜甚樂。

translations.literal: Kejia memorialized: "Before Yao had obtained Shun he had worry for himself; once he had obtained Shun, he should naturally have been greatly pleased."
translations.idiomatic: Kejia replied, "Before Yao found Shun he had worries of his own; once he had Shun, he could only rejoice."

sentences.zh: 」允文奏：「堯獨高五帝之壽以此。

translations.literal: Yunwen memorialized: "Yao alone surpassed the Five Emperors in longevity for this reason."
translations.idiomatic: Yunwen added, "It was for this reason that Yao alone outlived all the Five Emperors."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 」允文既罷相，克家獨秉政，雖近戚權幸不少假借，而外濟以和。

translations.literal: After Yunwen was dismissed as chancellor, Kejia alone held the government. Though he did not grant much leeway to close relatives and favorites, outwardly he supplemented this with harmony.
translations.idiomatic: After Yunwen was dismissed, Kejia held the government alone. He granted little favor to relatives and court favorites, yet outwardly tempered his firmness with conciliation.

sentences.zh: 張說入樞府，公議不與，寢命，俄復用。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue entered the Bureau of Military Affairs; public opinion did not support it, and the appointment was shelved, but soon he was used again.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhang Yue was appointed to the Bureau of Military Affairs, public opinion opposed it and the order was shelved — yet soon he was reappointed.

sentences.zh: 說怒士夫不附己，謀中傷之，克家悉力調護，善類賴之。

translations.literal: Zhang Yue was angry that scholars did not attach themselves to him and plotted to slander them. Kejia exerted all his strength to mediate and protect them, and men of integrity relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yue resented that scholars would not rally to him and plotted to ruin them. Kejia did everything in his power to protect them, and men of integrity owed their safety to him.

sentences.zh: 議金使朝見授書儀，時欲移文對境以正其禮，克家議不合，遂求去，以觀文殿大學士知建康府。

translations.literal: When deliberating on the ceremony for Jin envoys' presentation of letters at court audience, the court at the time wished to send an official communication across the border to correct their protocol. Kejia disagreed with this and then requested to leave, and was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Prefect of Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: When the court debated the ceremony for Jin envoys presenting letters at audience, some wished to send an official communication across the border to correct their protocol. Kejia disagreed, resigned, and was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture and Prefect of Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 陛辭，上以治效為問，克家勸上無求奇功。

translations.literal: At his audience of leave-taking the emperor asked about governing achievements, and Kejia urged the emperor not to seek extraordinary accomplishments.
translations.idiomatic: At his farewell audience the emperor asked about his governing record, and Kejia urged him not to pursue spectacular achievements.

sentences.zh: 既而三省、密院卒移牒泗州，敵不從，遣泛使來，舉朝震駭。

translations.literal: Before long the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs still sent a dispatch to Sizhou; the enemy did not comply and sent a general envoy, and the whole court was shaken.
translations.idiomatic: Before long the Three Departments and the Bureau of Military Affairs sent a dispatch to Sizhou anyway. The enemy refused to comply and sent a general envoy, and the whole court was shaken.

sentences.zh: 後二年，湯邦彥坐使事貶，天下益服克家謀國之忠。

translations.literal: Two years later Tang Bangyan was demoted on account of his mission, and all under Heaven came increasingly to respect Kejia's loyal statecraft.
translations.idiomatic: Two years later Tang Bangyan was demoted over his diplomatic mission, and the empire came increasingly to respect Kejia's loyal judgment in state affairs.

sentences.zh: 淳熙八年，起知福州，在鎮有治績。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Chunxi he was recalled to serve as prefect of Fuzhou and had governing achievements during his tenure.
translations.idiomatic: In 1181 he was recalled to serve as prefect of Fuzhou, where he achieved a solid governing record.

sentences.zh: 趙雄奏欲令再任，降旨仍知福州。

translations.literal: Zhao Xiong memorialized that he should be retained for another term, and an edict was issued keeping him as prefect of Fuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Xiong memorialized that Kejia should serve another term, and an edict was issued retaining him as prefect of Fuzhou.

sentences.zh: 召除醴泉觀使。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Commissioner of the Liquan Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to the capital and appointed Commissioner of the Liquan Palace.

sentences.zh: 九年九月，拜右丞相，封儀國公。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the ninth year he was appointed Right Grand Chancellor and enfeoffed as Duke of Yiguo.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the ninth year he was appointed Right Grand Chancellor and enfeoffed as Duke of Yiguo.

sentences.zh: 逾月而疾。

translations.literal: After more than a month he fell ill.
translations.idiomatic: After little more than a month he fell ill.

sentences.zh: 十三年，命以內祠兼侍讀，賜第，在所存問不絕。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was ordered to hold an inner-court sinecure while concurrently serving as Reader-in-Waiting, was granted a residence, and inquiries from the court were unceasing.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was given an inner-court sinecure while concurrently serving as Reader-in-Waiting, granted an official residence, and the court's inquiries after his health never ceased.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月，薨，年六十。

translations.literal: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month of the fourteenth year he died, aged sixty.

sentences.zh: 手書遺奏，上為之垂涕，贈少師，諡「文靖」。

translations.literal: He left a final memorial in his own hand; the emperor wept for him and posthumously appointed him Junior Preceptor, with the posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He left a final memorial in his own hand. The emperor wept for him and posthumously appointed him Junior Preceptor, with the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 初，唱第時，孝宗由建邸入侍，愛其風度峻整，及登政府，眷寵尤渥。

translations.literal: At the outset, when he ranked at the palace examination, Xiaozong had entered the palace from the Jian estate and admired his stern, dignified bearing. When Kejia reached the government, favor and grace were especially ample.
translations.idiomatic: When he ranked at the palace examination, Xiaozong had just entered the palace from the Jian estate and admired his stern, dignified bearing. Once Kejia reached high office, imperial favor was especially generous.

sentences.zh: 為文渾厚明白，自成一家，辭命尤溫雅，多行於世。

translations.literal: His writing was full and clear, forming a school of its own; his edicts and commissions were especially warm and elegant and circulated widely in the world.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was full-bodied and lucid, forming a style of its own. His edicts and commissions were especially warm and elegant and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 汪澈，字明遠，自新安徙居饒州浮梁。

translations.literal: Wang Che, styled Mingyuan, moved from Xin'an to settle in Fuliang, Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Che, courtesy name Mingyuan, moved from Xin'an to settle in Fuliang in Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 第進士，教授衡州、沅州。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination and served as Erudite at Hengzhou and Yuanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination and served as Erudite at Hengzhou and Yuanzhou.

sentences.zh: 用万俟卨薦，為秘書正字、校書郎。

translations.literal: On the recommendation of Wan Qixie he became Corrector in the Secretariat and Collator.
translations.idiomatic: On Wan Qixie's recommendation he was appointed Corrector in the Secretariat and Collator.

sentences.zh: 輪對，乞令帥臣、監司、侍從、臺諫各舉將帥，高宗善之，行其言。

translations.literal: At a rotating audience he requested that commanders-in-chief, supervisory commissioners, attendant officials, and censor-remonstrators each recommend generals. Gaozong approved this and carried out his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: At a rotating audience he requested that commanders-in-chief, supervisory commissioners, attendant officials, and censor-remonstrators each recommend generals. Gaozong approved and implemented his proposal.

sentences.zh: 除監察御史，進殿中侍御史，特賜鞍馬。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor, advanced to Attendant Censor within the Palace, and specially granted saddle and horse.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Investigating Censor, promoted to Attendant Censor within the Palace, and specially granted saddle and horse.

sentences.zh: 時和戎歲久，邊防浸弛，澈陳養民養兵、自治豫備之說，累數千言。

translations.literal: At the time peace with the enemy had lasted many years and frontier defenses had gradually slackened. Che expounded his views on nurturing the people, nurturing troops, self-governance, and advance preparation, totaling several thousand characters.
translations.idiomatic: Peace with the enemy had lasted many years and frontier defenses had gradually slackened. Che set forth his views on nurturing the people, building up the army, self-governance, and advance preparation in a memorial of several thousand characters.

sentences.zh: 顯仁皇后攢宮訖役，議者欲廣四隅，士庶墳在二十里內皆當遷，命澈按視。

translations.literal: When construction at Empress Xianren's provisional tomb was completed, deliberators wished to expand the four corners, and commoners' graves within twenty li would all have had to be moved. Che was ordered to inspect on site.
translations.idiomatic: When construction at Empress Xianren's provisional tomb was completed, some proposed expanding the grounds on all four sides, which would have required relocating every commoner's grave within twenty li. Che was ordered to inspect the site.

sentences.zh: 還奏：「昭慈、徽宗、顯肅、懿節四陵舊占百步，已數十年，今日何為是紛紛？

translations.literal: Returning he memorialized: "The four tombs — Zhaoci, Huizong, Xiansu, and Yijie — long ago occupied a hundred paces and have stood thus for decades. Why raise such an uproar today?"
translations.idiomatic: On returning he memorialized, "The four tombs — Zhaoci, Huizong, Xiansu, and Yijie — have occupied a hundred paces for decades. Why make such a fuss today?"

sentences.zh: 漢長樂、未央宮夾樗裡疾墓，未嘗遷。

translations.literal: In Han times Changle and Weiyang palaces stood beside the tombs of Chunyu Ji without relocating them.
translations.idiomatic: In Han times the Changle and Weiyang palaces stood beside the tomb of Chunyu Ji without anyone demanding its removal.

sentences.zh: 國朝宮陵儀制，在封堠界內，不許開故合祔，願遷出者聽，其意深矣。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's ritual system for imperial tomb-palaces, within the boundary mounds, does not permit opening old graves for joint burial; those who wish to move out may do so — the intent is profound.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's ritual system for imperial tomb-palaces forbids opening old graves for joint burial within the boundary mounds, though those who wish to relocate may do so — the intent is deeply considered.

sentences.zh: 」高宗大悟，悉如舊。

translations.literal: Gaozong understood completely and restored everything as before.
translations.idiomatic: Gaozong fully understood and restored everything as it had been.

sentences.zh: 葉義問使金還，頗知犯邊謀，澈言：「不素備，事至倉卒，靖康之變可鑒。

translations.literal: Ye Yiwen returned from a mission to Jin and learned much of border-incursion plans. Che said: "Without prior preparation, when matters arrive in haste, the Jingkang disaster stands as a warning."
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yiwen returned from a mission to Jin having learned much of their border-incursion plans. Che said, "Without prior preparation, when crisis strikes suddenly, the Jingkang disaster stands as a warning."

sentences.zh: 今將驕卒惰，宜加蒐閱，使有鬥心。

translations.literal: Today generals are arrogant and troops lax; training and inspection should be increased to give them fighting spirit.
translations.idiomatic: Today the generals are arrogant and the troops slack. Training and inspection should be intensified to restore their fighting spirit.

sentences.zh: 文武職事務選實才，不限資格。

translations.literal: Civil and military posts should all select men of real talent, without limiting by seniority requirements.
translations.idiomatic: Civil and military appointments should go to men of real ability, without restriction by seniority or formal qualifications.

sentences.zh: 」除侍御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 左相湯思退不協人望，澈同殿中侍御史陳俊卿劾罷，又論鎮江大將劉寶十罪，詔奪節予祠。

translations.literal: Left Grand Councillor Tang Situi did not accord with popular expectation. Che, together with Attendant Censor within the Palace Chen Junqing, impeached and removed him. He also charged Liu Bao, the great general at Zhenjiang, with ten crimes; an edict stripped him of his tally and granted him a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: Left Grand Councillor Tang Situi had lost public confidence. Che, together with Attendant Censor Chen Junqing, impeached and removed him. He also charged Liu Bao, the great general at Zhenjiang, with ten crimes; an edict stripped him of his command tally and granted him a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，上元前一夕，風雷雨雪交作，澈言《春秋》魯隱公時大雷震電，繼以雨雪，孔子以八日之間再有大變，謹而書之。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, on the eve of the Lantern Festival, wind, thunder, rain, and snow occurred together. Che cited that in the Spring and Autumn Annals, during the time of Duke Yin of Lu, great thunder and lightning were followed by rain and snow, and Confucius, because within eight days there were two great changes, recorded them with care.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, on the eve of the Lantern Festival, wind, thunder, rain, and snow struck together. Che cited the Spring and Autumn Annals: during the reign of Duke Yin of Lu, great thunder and lightning were followed by rain and snow, and because two great portents occurred within eight days, Confucius recorded them with particular care.

sentences.zh: 今一夕間二異交至，此陰盛之證，殆為金人。

translations.literal: Now within one night two portents arrived together — this is evidence of yin in excess and likely concerns the Jin people.
translations.idiomatic: Now two portents have arrived in a single night — a sign of yin in excess, and likely a warning concerning the Jin.

sentences.zh: 今荊、襄無統督，江海乏備禦，因陳修攘十二事。

translations.literal: Currently Jing and Xiang have no overall commander, and river and sea defenses lack preparedness. He thereupon set forth twelve measures for defense and recovery.
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Xiang currently have no overall commander, and river and sea defenses are unprepared. He thereupon set forth twelve measures for defense and recovery.

sentences.zh: 殿帥楊存中久握兵權，內結閹寺，王十朋、陳俊卿等繼論其罪，高宗欲存護使去，澈與俊卿同具奏，存中始罷。

translations.literal: Palace Commander Yang Cunzhong had long held military power and colluded inwardly with eunuchs. Wang Shipeng, Chen Junqing, and others successively charged his crimes. Gaozong wished to protect him and have him leave office. Che and Junqing jointly submitted a memorial, and only then was Cunzhong dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Palace Commander Yang Cunzhong had long held military power and cultivated ties with eunuchs. Wang Shipeng, Chen Junqing, and others successively charged him with crimes. Gaozong wished to protect him and ease him out of office, but Che and Junqing jointly submitted a memorial, and only then was Cunzhong dismissed.

sentences.zh: 會金使高景山來求釁端，澈言：「天下之勢，強弱無定形，在吾所以用之。

translations.literal: When Jin envoy Gao Jingshan came seeking grounds for provocation, Che said: "The balance of power under Heaven has no fixed form; it lies in how we employ it."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin envoy Gao Jingshan came seeking grounds for provocation, Che said, "The balance of power under Heaven has no fixed shape — it depends on how we use it."

sentences.zh: 陛下屈己和戎，厚遺金繒，彼輒出惡言，以撼吾國。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has humbled himself to make peace and sent rich gifts of gold and silk, yet they repeatedly utter hostile words to shake our state.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty has humbled himself to make peace and sent rich gifts of gold and silk, yet they repeatedly utter hostile words to undermine our state.

sentences.zh: 願陛下赫然睿斷，益兵嚴備，佈告中外，將見上下一心，其氣百倍矣。

translations.literal: I hope Your Majesty will rise to a resolute and luminous decision, increase troops and tighten defenses, and proclaim this within and without — then upper and lower will be of one mind and their spirit will be multiplied a hundredfold.
translations.idiomatic: I hope Your Majesty will act with resolute wisdom, increase troops and tighten defenses, and proclaim this throughout the realm — then court and country will unite and their morale will be multiplied a hundredfold.

sentences.zh: 」除御史中丞。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 尋遣馬帥成閔以所部三萬人屯荊、襄，以澈為湖北、京西宣諭使，詔凡吏能否、民利病悉以聞。

translations.literal: Soon the cavalry commander Cheng Min was dispatched with thirty thousand men of his command to garrison Jing and Xiang, and Che was made Pacification Commissioner for Hubei and Jingxi. An edict ordered that all officials' competence and all people's benefits and harms be reported.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the cavalry commander Cheng Min was dispatched with thirty thousand troops to garrison Jing and Xiang, and Che was appointed Pacification Commissioner for Hubei and Jingxi. An edict ordered him to report on officials' competence and the people's welfare.

sentences.zh: 過九江，王炎見澈論邊事，辟為屬，偕至襄陽撫諸軍。

translations.literal: Passing Jiujiang, Wang Yan met Che to discuss frontier affairs, recruited him as an aide, and together they went to Xiangyang to reassure the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Passing through Jiujiang, Wang Yan met Che to discuss frontier affairs, recruited him as an aide, and together they went to Xiangyang to reassure the troops.

sentences.zh: 鄂帥田師中老而怯，立奏易之。

translations.literal: E Prefect Tian Shizhong was old and timid; Che immediately memorialized to replace him.
translations.idiomatic: The commander at E Prefecture, Tian Shizhong, was old and timid; Che immediately memorialized for his replacement.

sentences.zh: 時欲置襄守荊南，澈奏：「襄陽地重，為荊楚門戶，不可棄。

translations.literal: At the time they wished to post the Xiangyang prefect to Jingnan. Che memorialized: "Xiangyang's territory is weighty — it is the gateway of Jing-Chu and must not be abandoned."
translations.idiomatic: At the time the court wished to transfer the Xiangyang prefect to Jingnan. Che memorialized, "Xiangyang is strategically vital — the gateway to Jing-Chu — and must not be abandoned."

sentences.zh: 」敵將劉萼擁眾十萬，揚聲欲取荊南，又欲分軍自光、黃搗武昌。

translations.literal: The enemy general Liu E commanded a hundred thousand men, proclaiming intent to take Jingnan, and also planned to divide forces from Guang and Huang to strike Wuchang.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy general Liu E commanded a hundred thousand men, proclaiming his intent to take Jingnan while also planning to divide his forces from Guang and Huang to strike Wuchang.

sentences.zh: 朝廷以敵昔由此入江南，令吳拱嚴護武昌津渡。

translations.literal: The court, because the enemy had once entered Jiangnan by this route, ordered Wu Gong to guard Wuchang's ferry crossings strictly.
translations.idiomatic: Because the enemy had once entered Jiangnan by this route, the court ordered Wu Gong to guard Wuchang's ferry crossings strictly.

sentences.zh: 拱將引兵加鄂，澈聞之，馳書止拱，而自發鄂之餘兵戍黃州，俾拱留襄。

translations.literal: Gong was about to lead troops to reinforce E Prefecture. Che heard of this, sent urgent letters to stop Gong, and himself mobilized E's remaining troops to garrison Huangzhou, causing Gong to remain at Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Gong was about to lead troops to reinforce E Prefecture. Che heard of this, sent urgent letters to stop him, and himself mobilized E's remaining troops to garrison Huangzhou, keeping Gong at Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 敵騎奄至樊城，拱大戰漢水上，敵眾敗走。

translations.literal: Enemy cavalry suddenly reached Fancheng. Gong fought a great battle on the Han River and the enemy host was routed.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy cavalry suddenly reached Fancheng. Gong fought a great battle on the Han River and routed the enemy host.

sentences.zh: 時唐、鄧、陳、蔡、汝、潁相次歸職方。

translations.literal: At the time Tang, Deng, Chen, Cai, Ru, and Ying successively returned to the jurisdiction of the Ministry of Works.
translations.idiomatic: Tang, Deng, Chen, Cai, Ru, and Ying successively returned to Song control.

sentences.zh: 未幾，金主亮死，澈乞出兵淮甸，與荊、襄軍夾擊其歸師。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Hailing of Jin died. Che requested dispatching troops to the Huai region to join with the Jing and Xiang armies in a pincer attack on the enemy's returning forces.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Hailing of Jin died. Che requested dispatching troops to the Huai region to join with the Jing and Xiang armies in a pincer attack on the enemy's retreating forces.

sentences.zh: 未報，而金新主罷兵請和，召澈入為參知政事，與宰相陳康伯同贊內禪。

translations.literal: Before a reply came, the new Jin ruler ceased hostilities and sued for peace. Che was summoned to serve as Vice Grand Councillor and, together with Chief Minister Chen Kangbo, assisted in the abdication and transfer of rule.
translations.idiomatic: Before a reply came, the new Jin ruler ceased hostilities and sued for peace. Che was summoned to serve as Vice Grand Councillor and, together with Chief Minister Chen Kangbo, assisted in the internal transfer of the throne.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，入奏，還武昌，而張浚克期大舉，詔澈出師應之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing he entered court to memorialize, returned to Wuchang, and when Zhang Jun set a date for a major campaign, an edict ordered Che to take the field in response.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing he entered court to memorialize, returned to Wuchang, and when Zhang Jun set a date for a major campaign, an edict ordered Che to take the field in support.

sentences.zh: 澈以議不合，乞令浚並領荊、襄。

translations.literal: Che, because deliberations did not agree, requested that Jun be given concurrent command over Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Che, finding himself at odds with the plan, requested that Zhang Jun be given concurrent command over Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 諫議大夫王大寶論澈無制勝策，皇甫倜以忠義結山砦，扼敵要衝，澈不能節制，坐視孤軍墮敵計。

translations.literal: Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Wang Dabao charged that Che had no strategy for victory. Huangfu Tong had rallied mountain forts through loyalty and righteousness and blocked the enemy's vital route, yet Che could not control matters and sat watching an isolated army fall into the enemy's plan.
translations.idiomatic: Remonstrance and Discussion Grandee Wang Dabao charged that Che had no strategy for victory. Huangfu Tong had rallied mountain forts through loyalty and righteousness and blocked a vital enemy route, yet Che could not coordinate the effort and sat by while an isolated force fell into the enemy's trap.

sentences.zh: 趙撙以千五百人救方城，敗散五百餘人，澈漫不加省。

translations.literal: Zhao Zun with fifteen hundred men went to relieve Fangcheng; more than five hundred were defeated and scattered, yet Che casually did not investigate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Zun led fifteen hundred men to relieve Fangcheng; more than five hundred were defeated and scattered, yet Che made no inquiry whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 乞罷黜。

translations.literal: He requested dismissal.
translations.idiomatic: He requested Che's dismissal.

sentences.zh: 澈亦請祠，除資政殿學士、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Che also requested a sinecure and was appointed Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance and Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Che also requested a sinecure and was appointed Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance and Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 大寶疏再上，落職，仍祠祿。

translations.literal: Wang Dabao submitted another memorial; Che was demoted from office but still retained his stipend.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Dabao submitted another memorial; Che was demoted from office but retained his stipend.

sentences.zh: 明年，知建康府，尋除樞密使。

translations.literal: The next year he served as Prefect of Jiankang, and soon was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he served as Prefect of Jiankang, and soon was appointed Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 在位二年，以觀文殿學士奉洞霄祠，尋知鄂州兼安撫使。

translations.literal: After two years in office he served the Tongxiao sinecure as Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, and soon was Prefect of E Prefecture with concurrent Pacification Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: After two years in office he took up the Tongxiao sinecure as Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, and soon was appointed Prefect of E Prefecture with concurrent Pacification Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 孝宗訪邊事，澈奏：「向者我有唐、鄧為藩籬，又皇甫倜控扼陳、蔡，敵不敢窺襄。

translations.literal: Xiaozong inquired about frontier affairs. Che memorialized: "Formerly we had Tang and Deng as outer barriers, and Huangfu Tong controlled Chen and Cai; the enemy did not dare gaze toward Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong inquired about frontier affairs, Che memorialized, "Formerly we had Tang and Deng as outer barriers, and Huangfu Tong controlled Chen and Cai — the enemy did not dare threaten Xiangyang."

sentences.zh: 既失兩郡，倜復內徙，敵屯新野，相距百里爾。

translations.literal: Once we lost the two prefectures and Tong was transferred inward, the enemy encamped at Xinye — barely a hundred li apart.
translations.idiomatic: Once we lost those two prefectures and Tong was transferred inward, the enemy encamped at Xinye — barely a hundred li away.

sentences.zh: 臣令趙撙、王宣築城儲糧，分備要害，有以待敵。

translations.literal: I have ordered Zhao Zun and Wang Xuan to build walls and store grain and to garrison key points separately, so we may await the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: I have ordered Zhao Zun and Wang Xuan to build walls, stockpile grain, and garrison key points, so we may be ready when the enemy comes.

sentences.zh: 至於機會之來，難以豫料。

translations.literal: As for when opportunity may come, that is hard to foretell.
translations.idiomatic: As for when opportunity may arise, that is impossible to predict in advance.

sentences.zh: 」孝宗善之。

translations.literal: Xiaozong approved this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiaozong approved.

sentences.zh: 時議廢江州軍，澈言不可。

translations.literal: At the time there was deliberation on abolishing the Jiangzhou army; Che said this could not be done.
translations.idiomatic: At the time there was debate over abolishing the Jiangzhou army; Che argued against it.

sentences.zh: 知寧國府，改福州、福建安撫使，復請祠。

translations.literal: He served as Prefect of Ningguo, was transferred to Fuzhou as Fujian Pacification Commissioner, and again requested a sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Prefect of Ningguo, was transferred to Fuzhou as Fujian Pacification Commissioner, and again requested a sinecure.

sentences.zh: 尋致仕。

translations.literal: Soon he retired.
translations.idiomatic: He soon retired from office.

sentences.zh: 卒，年六十三。

translations.literal: He died, aged sixty-three.
translations.idiomatic: He died, aged sixty-three.

sentences.zh: 贈金紫光祿大夫，諡「莊敏」。

translations.literal: He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the posthumous title Zhuangmin.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously appointed Grand Master of the Golden Seal and Purple Ribbon, with the posthumous title Zhuangmin.

sentences.zh: 澈為殿中日，薦陳俊卿、王十朋、陳之茂為臺官，高宗曰：「名士也，次第用之矣。

translations.literal: When Che served in the Palace Bureau, he recommended Chen Junqing, Wang Shipeng, and Chen Zhimao for censorial posts. Gaozong said: "Men of renown — they will be used in turn."
translations.idiomatic: When Che served in the Palace Bureau, he recommended Chen Junqing, Wang Shipeng, and Chen Zhimao for censorial posts. Gaozong said, "Men of renown — they will be appointed in due course."

sentences.zh: 」在樞府，孝宗密訪人材，薦百有十八人。

translations.literal: In the Bureau of Military Affairs, when Xiaozong secretly inquired about talent, he recommended one hundred eighteen men.
translations.idiomatic: In the Bureau of Military Affairs, when Xiaozong privately inquired about talent, he recommended one hundred eighteen men.

sentences.zh: 嘗奏言：「臣起寒遠，所以報國惟無私不欺爾。

translations.literal: He once memorialized: "I rose from humble and remote origins; my way of repaying the state is nothing but to be without selfishness and without deception."
translations.idiomatic: He once memorialized, "I rose from humble and remote origins; the only way I can repay the state is to serve without selfishness and without deception."

sentences.zh: 」其自奉清約，雖貴猶布衣時。

translations.literal: In his personal conduct he was frugal and austere; even when ennobled he lived as in his commoner days.
translations.idiomatic: In his personal life he was frugal and austere; even when ennobled he lived as simply as in his commoner days.

sentences.zh: 有文集二十卷、奏議十二卷。

translations.literal: He left collected works in twenty juan and memorials in twelve juan.
translations.idiomatic: He left collected works in twenty juan and memorials in twelve juan.

sentences.zh: 葉義問

translations.literal: Ye Yiwen
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yiwen

sentences.zh: 葉義問，字審言，嚴州壽昌人。

translations.literal: Ye Yiwen, styled Shenyan, was a native of Shouchang in Yan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yiwen, courtesy name Shenyan, was a native of Shouchang in Yan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，登進士第。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Jianyan era he passed the jinshi examination.
