translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Jianyan era he passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 調臨安府司理參軍。

translations.literal: He was assigned as Judicial Administrator of Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was assigned as Judicial Administrator of Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 范宗尹為相，義問與沈長卿等疏其姦。

translations.literal: When Fan Zongyin was chief minister, Yiwen together with Shen Changqing and others submitted a memorial exposing his wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: When Fan Zongyin served as chief minister, Yiwen together with Shen Changqing and others submitted a memorial exposing his corruption.

sentences.zh: 為饒州教授，攝郡。

translations.literal: He served as Erudite of Raozhou and administered the prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Erudite of Raozhou and administered prefectural affairs.

sentences.zh: 歲旱，以便宜發常平米振民，提刑黃敦書劾之，詔勿問。

translations.literal: In a drought year he expediently released ever-normal granary rice to relieve the people. Intendant Huang Dunshu impeached him, but an edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.
translations.idiomatic: During a drought he expediently released ever-normal granary rice to relieve the people. Intendant Huang Dunshu impeached him, but an edict ordered that the matter not be pursued.

sentences.zh: 前樞密徐俯門僧犯罪，義問繩以法，俯嘗舉義問，怒甚，乃袖薦書還之。

translations.literal: A monk at the gate of former Commissioner Xu Fu committed a crime; Yiwen bound him by law. Xu had once recommended Yiwen and was greatly angered, and returned the recommendation letter in his sleeve.
translations.idiomatic: A monk at the gate of former Commissioner Xu Fu committed a crime; Yiwen prosecuted him by law. Xu had once recommended Yiwen and was furious, returning the recommendation letter from his sleeve.

sentences.zh: 知江寧縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Jiangning County.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Jiangning County.

sentences.zh: 召秦檜所親役，同僚不可，義問曰：「釋是則何以服他人。

translations.literal: He summoned corvée laborers who were Qin Hui's intimates; colleagues objected, but Yiwen said: "If I release these, how can I make others submit?"
translations.idiomatic: He summoned corvée laborers who were Qin Hui's intimates; colleagues objected, but Yiwen said, "If I release these men, how can I enforce the law on anyone else?"

sentences.zh: 」卒役之。

translations.literal: In the end he put them to labor service.
translations.idiomatic: In the end he put them to corvée labor.

sentences.zh: 通判江州。

translations.literal: He served as Vice Prefect of Jiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as Vice Prefect of Jiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 豫章守張宗元忤檜，或中以飛語，事下漕臣張常先。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyuan, prefect of Yuzhang, had offended Qin Hui; someone struck at him with slanderous talk, and the matter was referred to Transport Commissioner Zhang Changxian.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyuan, prefect of Yuzhang, had offended Qin Hui; someone attacked him with slander, and the matter was referred to Transport Commissioner Zhang Changxian.

sentences.zh: 宗元道九江，常先檄義問拘其舟，義問投檄曰：「吾寧得罪，不為不祥。

translations.literal: Zhang Zongyuan passed Jiujiang; Changxian issued an order for Yiwen to detain his boat. Yiwen returned the order, saying: "I would rather incur guilt than commit an inauspicious act."
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zongyuan passed through Jiujiang; Changxian ordered Yiwen to detain his boat. Yiwen returned the order, saying, "I would rather face punishment than commit an unjust act."

sentences.zh: 」常先白檜，罷去。

translations.literal: Changxian reported to Qin Hui, and Yiwen was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Changxian reported to Qin Hui, and Yiwen was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 檜死，湯思退薦之，上記其嘗言范宗尹，召至，言臺諫廢置在人主，檜親黨宜盡罷逐，以言得罪者宜敘復。

translations.literal: After Qin Hui died, Tang Situi recommended him; the emperor remembered that he had spoken against Fan Zongyin and summoned him. He said that appointing and dismissing censor-remonstrators rested with the ruler, that Qin Hui's partisans should all be dismissed, and that men punished for speaking out should be rehabilitated.
translations.idiomatic: After Qin Hui died, Tang Situi recommended him; the emperor remembered his memorial against Fan Zongyin and summoned him. He argued that appointing and dismissing censor-remonstrators rested with the ruler, that Qin Hui's partisans should all be removed, and that men punished for speaking out should be rehabilitated.

sentences.zh: 擢殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was elevated to Attendant Censor within the Palace.
translations.idiomatic: He was elevated to Attendant Censor within the Palace.

sentences.zh: 樞密湯鵬舉效檜所為，植其黨周方崇、李庚，置籍臺諫，鉏異己者。

translations.literal: Commissioner Tang Pengju imitated Qin Hui's methods, planted his partisans Zhou Fangchong and Li Geng, registered censor-remonstrators, and rooted out dissenters.
translations.idiomatic: Commissioner Tang Pengju imitated Qin Hui's methods, planted his partisans Zhou Fangchong and Li Geng, registered censor-remonstrators, and purged dissenters.

sentences.zh: 義問累章劾鵬舉，有「一檜死一檜生」之語，並方崇等皆罷之。

translations.literal: Yiwen repeatedly memorialized to impeach Pengju, with the words "one Qin Hui dead, one Qin Hui alive," and Fangchong and others were all dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Yiwen repeatedly memorialized to impeach Pengju, declaring "one Qin Hui dead, one Qin Hui alive," and Fangchong and the others were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 又言：「凡擇將遇一闕，令樞密院具三名取上旨，則軍政盡出掌握。

translations.literal: He also said: "Whenever selecting a general for a vacancy, have the Bureau of Military Affairs submit three names for the emperor's decision — then military affairs will all be under imperial control."
translations.idiomatic: He also argued, "Whenever a general's post falls vacant, the Bureau of Military Affairs should submit three names for the emperor's choice — then military affairs will remain under imperial control."

sentences.zh: 」 遷侍御史。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 朱樸、沈虛中奉祠里居，義問劾其附秦檜，皆移居。

translations.literal: Zhu Pu and Shen Xuzhong were serving temple sinecures at home; Yiwen impeached them for attaching themselves to Qin Hui, and both were ordered to relocate.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Pu and Shen Xuzhong were serving temple sinecures at home; Yiwen impeached them for having attached themselves to Qin Hui, and both were ordered to relocate.

sentences.zh: 郊祀赦，義問言：「頃歲附會告訐者，不應例移放。

translations.literal: At the suburban-sacrifice amnesty, Yiwen said: "Those in recent years who followed suit in informing and denouncing should not be moved under general release."
translations.idiomatic: At the suburban-sacrifice amnesty, Yiwen argued that those who in recent years had joined in informing and denouncing should not be released under the general amnesty.

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 遷吏部侍郎兼史館修撰，尋兼侍讀，拜同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent Compiler in the History Institute, soon also Reader-in-Waiting, and appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to Vice Minister of Personnel with concurrent Compiler in the History Institute, soon also Reader-in-Waiting, and appointed Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上聞金有犯邊意，遣義問奉使覘之，還奏：「彼造舟船，備器械，其用心必有所在，宜屯駐沿海要害備之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard that Jin had intent to invade the frontier and dispatched Yiwen on a mission to observe. Returning he memorialized: "They are building ships and preparing weapons; their intent must lie somewhere. Coastal key points should be garrisoned in preparation."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that Jin intended to invade the frontier, the emperor dispatched Yiwen on an observation mission. On returning he memorialized, "They are building ships and preparing weapons — their intent must be hostile. Coastal key points should be garrisoned in preparation."

sentences.zh: 」金主亮果南侵。

translations.literal: Emperor Hailing of Jin indeed invaded south.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Hailing of Jin did indeed invade south.

sentences.zh: 命視師，義問素不習軍旅，會劉錡捷書至，讀之至「金賊又添生兵」，顧吏曰：「『生兵』何物耶？

translations.literal: He was ordered to inspect the armies. Yiwen had never studied military affairs. When Liu Qi's victory dispatch arrived, he read as far as "the Jin bandits have added fresh troops" and turned to an attendant, saying: "What is 'fresh troops'?"
translations.idiomatic: He was ordered to inspect the armies. Yiwen had never studied military affairs. When Liu Qi's victory dispatch arrived, he read as far as "the Jin bandits have added fresh troops" and turned to a clerk, asking, "What are 'fresh troops'?"

sentences.zh: 」聞者掩口。

translations.literal: Those who heard covered their mouths.
translations.idiomatic: Those who heard stifled their laughter.

sentences.zh: 至鎮江，聞瓜洲官軍與敵相持，大失措，乃役民掘沙溝，植木枝為鹿角禦敵，一夕潮生，沙溝平，木枝盡去。

translations.literal: Reaching Zhenjiang he heard that the Guazhou army was locked in stalemate with the enemy and was greatly thrown off balance. He conscripted the people to dig sand trenches and planted wooden branches as abatis against the enemy. Overnight the tide rose, the sand trenches were levelled, and the branches were all swept away.
translations.idiomatic: Reaching Zhenjiang he heard that the Guazhou army was locked in stalemate with the enemy and panicked. He conscripted civilians to dig sand trenches and planted wooden branches as abatis. Overnight the tide rose, the trenches were filled in, and the branches were swept away.

sentences.zh: 會建康留守張燾遣人告急，義問乃遵陸，云往建康催發軍，市人皆媟罵之。

translations.literal: When Jiankang Intendant Zhang Tao sent someone with urgent news, Yiwen took the overland route, saying he was going to Jiankang to urge dispatch of troops. Market people all cursed him scornfully.
translations.idiomatic: When Jiankang Intendant Zhang Tao sent an urgent appeal, Yiwen took the overland route, claiming he was going to Jiankang to urge troop dispatch. Market people cursed him openly.

sentences.zh: 又聞敵據瓜洲，采石兵甚眾，復欲還鎮江，諸軍喧沸曰：「不可回矣，回則有不測。

translations.literal: Hearing again that the enemy held Guazhou and that Caishi had very many troops, he wished again to return to Zhenjiang. The armies clamored: "We cannot turn back; if we turn back there will be unpredictable consequences."
translations.idiomatic: Hearing that the enemy held Guazhou and that Caishi had a large force, he wished to return to Zhenjiang. The troops clamored, "We cannot turn back — if we do, the consequences are unpredictable."

sentences.zh: 」遂趨建康。

translations.literal: He then hastened to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: He then hastened to Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 已而金主亮被弑，師退，義問還朝，力請退，遂罷。

translations.literal: Before long Emperor Hailing of Jin was assassinated and the armies withdrew. Yiwen returned to court, strenuously requested to retire, and was dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Emperor Hailing of Jin was assassinated and the armies withdrew. Yiwen returned to court, strenuously requested retirement, and was dismissed.

sentences.zh: 隆興元年，中丞辛次膺論義問「頃護諸將幾敗事，且以官私其親」。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longxing Vice Censor-in-Chief Xin Ciying charged Yiwen with "having nearly ruined matters while overseeing the generals, and using his office for private benefit to relatives."
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Longxing, Vice Censor-in-Chief Xin Ciying charged that Yiwen "had nearly ruined matters while overseeing the generals, and used his office to favor relatives."

sentences.zh: 謫饒州。

translations.literal: He was demoted to Raozhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was demoted to Raozhou.

sentences.zh: 乾道元年，詔自便。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qiandao an edict restored him to free movement.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Qiandao an edict restored him to free movement.

sentences.zh: 六年卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he died, aged seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 蔣芾，字子禮，常州宜興人，之奇曾孫。

translations.literal: Jiang Fei, styled Zili, was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture and a great-grandson of Zhiqi.
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Fei, courtesy name Zili, was a native of Yixing in Chang Prefecture and a great-grandson of Zhiqi.

sentences.zh: 紹興二十一年，進士第二人。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year of Shaoxing he ranked second among jinshi graduates.
translations.idiomatic: In 1151 he ranked second among jinshi graduates.

sentences.zh: 孝宗即位，累遷起居郎兼直學士院。

translations.literal: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he rose through successive appointments to Recorder of the Left and concurrent Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiaozong succeeded to the throne, he rose through successive appointments to Recorder of the Left and concurrent Attendant of the Academy of Scholarly Worthies.

sentences.zh: 時宦者梁珂事上潛邸，撓權，尹穡論珂，與祠，芾繳奏罷之。

translations.literal: At the time eunuch Liang Ke had served Xiaozong when he was still heir apparent and encroached on power. Yin Ji impeached Ke and had him given a temple sinecure; Fei submitted a rescript memorial and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: At the time eunuch Liang Ke had served Xiaozong at the heir apparent's residence and encroached on power. Yin Ji impeached Ke and had him given a temple sinecure; Fei submitted a rescript memorial and had him dismissed.

sentences.zh: 簽書樞密院事，首奏加意邊防，又奏：「拔將才行伍間，識其姓名，一旦披籍可立取具。

translations.literal: As Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, his first memorial urged attention to frontier defense. He also memorialized: "Promote generals from among the ranks, record their names, and when the registers are opened they can be summoned at once."
translations.idiomatic: As Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, his first memorial urged attention to frontier defense. He also memorialized, "Promote generals from the ranks, record their names, and when registers are opened they can be summoned immediately."

sentences.zh: 又料簡歸正人，仍以北人將之，或令深入山東，或令自荊、襄深入。」

translations.literal: Also screen returned loyalists and still assign northerners to command them — some to drive deep into Shandong, some to penetrate deeply from Jing and Xiang."
translations.idiomatic: He also proposed screening returned loyalists and assigning northerners to command them — some to drive deep into Shandong, others to penetrate from Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 除權參知政事、同知國用事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Acting Vice Grand Councillor and concurrent Vice Director of State Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Acting Vice Grand Councillor and concurrent Vice Director of State Affairs.

sentences.zh: 芾奏：「方今財最費於養兵，藝祖取天下，不過十五萬人。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "Today finances are consumed most by maintaining troops. When the Founder took the realm, he had no more than a hundred fifty thousand men."
translations.idiomatic: Fei memorialized, "Today the greatest expense is maintaining troops. When the Founder took the realm, he had no more than a hundred fifty thousand men."

sentences.zh: 紹興初，外有大敵，內有巨寇，然兵數亦不若今日之多。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shaoxing, though there was a great external enemy and huge internal bandits, troop numbers still did not exceed today's.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Shaoxing, though there was a great external enemy and major internal bandits, troop numbers still fell short of today's.

sentences.zh: 近見陳敏勇汰三千人，戚方汰四千人，然多是有官人，與以外任，請券錢、添借給如故，是減於內而添于外，何益？

translations.literal: Recently I see Chen Minyong reduced three thousand men and Qi Fang four thousand, yet most were men with official rank given external appointments and still requesting certificate money and supplemental allowances as before — reducing within while adding without, what benefit is there?
translations.idiomatic: Recently Chen Minyong reduced three thousand troops and Qi Fang four thousand, yet most were men with official rank given external appointments who still drew certificate money and supplemental allowances as before — reducing within while adding without. What benefit is there?

sentences.zh: 又招兵耗蠹愈甚，臣考核在內諸軍，每月逃亡事故，常不下四百人。

translations.literal: Moreover recruiting troops wastes resources ever more severely. My audit of armies within the capital finds monthly desertions and casualties regularly no fewer than four hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Recruiting troops wastes resources ever more severely. My audit of capital armies finds monthly desertions and casualties regularly exceed four hundred.

sentences.zh: 若權停招兵一年有半，俟財用稍足，招丁壯，不惟省費，又得兵精。

translations.literal: If recruiting is provisionally halted for a year and a half, and when finances are somewhat sufficient only strong young men are recruited, not only will costs be saved but the troops will be better.
translations.idiomatic: If recruiting is halted for a year and a half, and when finances recover only strong young men are recruited, costs will be saved and the army will be stronger.

sentences.zh: 」上悟。

translations.literal: The emperor understood.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor understood.

sentences.zh: 一日，因進呈邊報，上顧芾曰：「將來都督非卿不可。

translations.literal: One day, while presenting frontier reports, the emperor turned to Fei and said: "In future the overall commander must be you."
translations.idiomatic: One day, while presenting frontier reports, the emperor turned to Fei and said, "When the time comes, you alone can serve as overall commander."

sentences.zh: 」芾奏：「臣未嘗經歷兵間。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "Your subject has never experienced military affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Fei replied, "Your subject has never served in military affairs."

sentences.zh: 」又奏：「方今錢穀不足，兵士不練，將帥與臣不相識，願陛下更審思其人。

translations.literal: He also memorialized: "Today funds and grain are insufficient, soldiers are untrained, and generals do not know your subject. I hope Your Majesty will further consider the right man."
translations.idiomatic: He added, "Funds and grain are insufficient, soldiers are untrained, and the generals do not know me. I hope Your Majesty will choose more carefully."

sentences.zh: 」南郊禮畢，宰相葉顒、魏杞罷。

translations.literal: After the southern-suburb rites were completed, chief ministers Ye Yong and Wei Qi were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: After the southern-suburb rites, chief ministers Ye Yong and Wei Qi were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 芾采眾論，參己見，為《籌邊志》上之。

translations.literal: Fei collected public opinion, added his own views, and submitted the Frontier Planning Record.
translations.idiomatic: Fei collected public opinion, added his own views, and submitted his Frontier Planning Record.

sentences.zh: 明年，拜右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼樞密使。

translations.literal: The next year he was appointed Right Grand Counsellor, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was appointed Right Grand Counsellor, Grand Councillor of the Secretariat-Chancellery, and concurrent Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 會母疾卒，詔起復，拜左僕射，芾力辭。

translations.literal: When his mother fell gravely ill and died, an edict ordered mourning leave waived and he was appointed Left Grand Counsellor; Fei strenuously declined.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother fell gravely ill and died, an edict ordered him to leave mourning and appointed him Left Grand Counsellor; Fei strenuously declined.

sentences.zh: 有密旨欲今歲大舉，手詔廷臣議，或主和，或主恢復，使芾決之。

translations.literal: There was a secret order wishing for a major campaign this year; an imperial letter ordered court officials to debate, some advocating peace and some recovery, and Fei was to decide.
translations.idiomatic: A secret order wished for a major campaign that year; an imperial letter ordered court officials to debate peace versus recovery, with Fei to decide.

sentences.zh: 芾奏：「天時人事未至。

translations.literal: Fei memorialized: "Heaven's timing and human affairs have not yet arrived."
translations.idiomatic: Fei memorialized, "Heaven's timing and human affairs are not yet ripe."

sentences.zh: 」拂上意。

translations.literal: This went against the emperor's intent.
translations.idiomatic: This went against the emperor's intent.

sentences.zh: 服闋，除觀文殿大學士、知紹興府、提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: After mourning was completed he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Prefect of Shaoxing, and Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning he was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, Prefect of Shaoxing, and Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 尋以言者論，落職，建昌軍居住。

translations.literal: Soon on accusers' charges he was demoted from office and ordered to reside in Jianchang Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon accusers brought charges and he was demoted, ordered to reside in Jianchang Circuit.

sentences.zh: 期年，有旨自便。

translations.literal: After a full year an edict restored him to free movement.
translations.idiomatic: After a full year an edict restored him to free movement.

sentences.zh: 再提舉洞霄宮，卒。

translations.literal: Again Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace, he died.
translations.idiomatic: Again appointed Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace, he died.

sentences.zh: 芾始以言邊事結上知，不十年間致相位，終以不能任兵事受責，豈優於論議而劣於事功歟？

translations.literal: Fei at first won the emperor's trust through speaking on frontier affairs and reached the chancellorship within less than ten years, yet in the end was blamed for inability to handle military affairs — was he superior in debate but inferior in practical achievement?
translations.idiomatic: Fei first won the emperor's trust through frontier policy and reached the chancellorship in less than ten years, yet was ultimately blamed for inability to handle military affairs — was he better at debate than at practical achievement?

sentences.zh: 葉顒，字子昂，興化軍仙遊人。

translations.literal: Ye Yong, styled Zi'ang, was a native of Xianyou in Xinghua Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yong, courtesy name Zi'ang, was a native of Xianyou in Xinghua Circuit.

sentences.zh: 登紹興元年進士第，為廣州南海縣主簿，攝尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Shaoxing, served as Recorder of Nanhai County in Guang Prefecture, and administered as assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1131, served as Recorder of Nanhai County in Guang Prefecture, and administered as assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 盜發，州檄巡、尉同捕，巡檢獲盜十餘人，歸其勞於顒，顒曰：「掠美、欺君、幸賞，三者皆罪，不忍為也。

translations.literal: When bandits rose, the prefecture ordered patrol inspectors and assistant magistrates to capture them jointly. The patrol inspector seized more than ten bandits and attributed the credit to Yong. Yong said: "Stealing credit, deceiving the ruler, and hoping for reward — all three are crimes; I am unwilling to commit them."
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose, the prefecture ordered patrol inspectors and assistant magistrates to capture them jointly. The patrol inspector seized more than ten bandits and attributed the credit to Yong. Yong said, "Stealing credit, deceiving the ruler, and hoping for reward — all three are crimes. I will not commit them."

sentences.zh: 」帥曾開大善之。

translations.literal: The prefecture commander Zeng Kai greatly approved of this.
translations.idiomatic: Prefecture commander Zeng Kai greatly approved.

sentences.zh: 知信州貴溪縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Guixi County in Xin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Guixi County in Xin Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時詔行經界，郡議以上中下三等定田稅，顒請分為九等，守從之，令信之六邑以貴溪為式。

translations.literal: At the time an edict ordered the carrying out of the field-boundary survey; the prefecture proposed fixing land tax in upper, middle, and lower three grades. Yong requested division into nine grades; the prefect agreed and ordered the six districts of Xin to take Guixi as the model.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered a field-boundary survey; the prefecture proposed three tax grades. Yong requested nine grades; the prefect agreed and ordered the six districts of Xin to follow Guixi's model.

sentences.zh: 知紹興府上虞縣。

translations.literal: He served as magistrate of Shangyu County in Shaoxing Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He served as magistrate of Shangyu County in Shaoxing Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 凡繇役，令民自推貨力甲乙，不以付吏，民欣然皆以實應。

translations.literal: For all corvée duties he had the people themselves assess their wealth and strength in order, without entrusting this to clerks; the people gladly responded truthfully.
translations.idiomatic: For all corvée duties he had the people assess their own wealth and strength, without entrusting the task to clerks; the people gladly responded truthfully.

sentences.zh: 摧租各書其數與民，約使自持戶租至庭，親視其入，咸便之。

translations.literal: For rent collection he wrote each household's amount for the people, agreeing that they bring their rent receipts to the hall themselves, and he personally watched the receipt — all found this convenient.
translations.idiomatic: For rent collection he wrote each household's amount and had them bring their receipts to the hall in person, watching the intake himself — all found this convenient.

sentences.zh: 帥曹泳令今歲夏租先期送什之八，顒請少紓其期，泳怒。

translations.literal: Prefect Cao Yong ordered that this year's summer rent be delivered eight-tenths in advance; Yong requested a slight easing of the deadline and Yong was angered.
translations.idiomatic: Prefect Cao Yong ordered that year's summer rent delivered eight-tenths in advance; Yong requested a slight extension and Cao was angered.

sentences.zh: 及麥大熟，民輸租反為諸邑最，泳大喜，許薦於朝，顒固辭。

translations.literal: When wheat ripened abundantly the people's rent delivery was actually the best among all districts; Yong was greatly pleased, promised to recommend him to court, but Yong firmly declined.
translations.idiomatic: When wheat ripened abundantly, rent collection in his district ranked first among all counties; Cao was delighted and offered to recommend him to court, but Yong firmly declined.

sentences.zh: 賀允中薦顒靜退，遂召見，顒論國仇未復，中原之民日企鑾輿之返，其語剴切，高宗嘉納。

translations.literal: He Yunchong recommended Yong for his quiet integrity; he was summoned for audience. Yong spoke on the national enmity not yet avenged and how the people of the Central Plains daily long for the imperial carriage's return; his words were earnest and cutting, and Gaozong praised and accepted them.
translations.idiomatic: He Yunchong recommended Yong for his quiet integrity; he was summoned for audience. Yong spoke on the national enmity not yet avenged and how the people of the Central Plains daily longed for the emperor's return; his words were earnest, and Gaozong praised and accepted them.

sentences.zh: 除將作監簿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Registrar of the Directorate of Palace Buildings.

sentences.zh: 知處州，青田令陳光獻羨餘百萬，顒以所獻充所賦。

translations.literal: As prefect of Chuzhou, Chen Guang of Qingtian submitted a surplus of a million; Yong used what was submitted to meet the assessed levy.
translations.idiomatic: As prefect of Chuzhou, Chen Guang of Qingtian submitted a surplus of a million; Yong applied it toward the assessed levy.

sentences.zh: 湯思退之兄居處州，家奴屠酤犯禁，一繩以法，思退不悅。

translations.literal: Tang Situi's elder brother lived in Chuzhou; a household slave violated the prohibition on butchering and selling wine and was bound entirely by law; Situi was displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Tang Situi's elder brother lived in Chuzhou; a household slave violated the prohibition on butchering and selling wine and was prosecuted by law; Situi was displeased.

sentences.zh: 屬常州逋緡錢四十萬，守坐免，移顒知常州。

translations.literal: Changzhou owed forty thousand strings in arrears; the prefect was dismissed from office and Yong was transferred to serve as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Changzhou owed forty thousand strings in tax arrears; the prefect was dismissed and Yong was transferred to serve as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 金犯邊，高宗視師建康，道毗陵，顒賜對舟次，因言：「恢復莫先於將相，故相張浚久謫無恙，是天留以相陛下也。

translations.literal: When Jin invaded the frontier, Gaozong inspected the armies at Jiankang, passed through Piling, and granted Yong an audience aboard ship. He then said: "Recovery must begin with generals and ministers; former chancellor Zhang Jun, long demoted yet unharmed — Heaven has preserved him to serve Your Majesty."
translations.idiomatic: When Jin invaded the frontier, Gaozong inspected the armies at Jiankang, passed through Piling, and granted Yong an audience aboard ship. He said, "Recovery must begin with generals and ministers; former chancellor Zhang Jun, long demoted yet unharmed — Heaven has preserved him to serve Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」顒初至郡，無旬月儲，未一年餘緡錢二十萬。

translations.literal: When Yong first arrived at the prefecture there was less than a month's or ten days' stores; in less than a year there was a surplus of two hundred thousand strings.
translations.idiomatic: When Yong first arrived there was less than a month's supply in the treasury; within a year he accumulated a surplus of two hundred thousand strings.

sentences.zh: 或勸獻羨，顒曰：「名羨餘，非重征則橫斂，是民之膏血也，以利易賞，心實恥之。」

translations.literal: Some urged presenting surplus revenue. Yong said: "Called 'surplus' — unless it comes from heavy taxation it is extortion, and that is the people's lifeblood. To trade profit for commendation — my heart truly shames to do it."
translations.idiomatic: Some urged presenting surplus revenue. Yong said, "What is called 'surplus' — unless it comes from heavy taxation it is extortion, the people's lifeblood. To trade profit for commendation — my heart would be ashamed."

sentences.zh: 召為尚書郎，除右司。

translations.literal: He was summoned as a Bureau Director in the Department of State Affairs and appointed to the Right Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned as a Bureau Director in the Department of State Affairs and appointed to the Right Bureau.

sentences.zh: 詔求直言，顒上疏謂：「陛下以手足之至親，付州郡之重寄，是利一人害一方也。

translations.literal: An edict sought frank speech; Yong submitted a memorial saying: "Your Majesty entrusts the heavy charge of a prefecture and district to the closest kin — this benefits one person and harms a whole region."
translations.idiomatic: An edict sought frank speech; Yong submitted a memorial saying, "Your Majesty entrusts the heavy charge of a prefecture to the closest kin — this benefits one person and harms a whole region."

sentences.zh: 」人稱其直。

translations.literal: People praised his frankness.
translations.idiomatic: People praised his frankness.

sentences.zh: 除吏部侍郎，復權尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and again acted as Minister.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Personnel and again acted as Minister.

sentences.zh: 時七司弊事未去，上疏言選部所以為弊，乃與郎官編七司條例為一書，上嘉之，令刻板頒示。

translations.literal: At the time abuses in the seven bureaus had not been removed. He submitted a memorial on why the Selection Bureau became corrupt, then compiled the regulations of the seven bureaus into one book with bureau officials. The emperor praised this and ordered it carved on blocks and promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Abuses in the seven bureaus had not been removed. He submitted a memorial on why the Selection Bureau had become corrupt, then compiled the regulations of the seven bureaus into one book with bureau officials. The emperor praised it and ordered it carved on blocks and promulgated.

sentences.zh: 除端明殿學士，拜參知政事兼同知樞密院事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Illuminating Governance and Vice Grand Councillor with concurrent Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Academician of the Hall for Illuminating Governance and Vice Grand Councillor with concurrent Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 武臣梁俊彥請稅沙田、蘆場，帝以問顒，對曰：「沙田乃江濱地，田隨沙漲而出沒不常，蘆場則臣未之詳也。

translations.literal: Military official Liang Junyan requested taxing sand fields and reed marshes. The emperor asked Yong, who replied: "Sand fields are riverside land; fields appear and vanish with sand buildup and are not constant. As for reed marshes, your subject is not well informed."
translations.idiomatic: Military official Liang Junyan requested taxing sand fields and reed marshes. The emperor asked Yong, who replied, "Sand fields are riverside land that appears and vanishes with shifting sand and is not constant. As for reed marshes, I am not well informed."

sentences.zh: 且辛巳軍興蘆場田租並復，今沙田不勝其擾。

translations.literal: Moreover at the Xinsi military emergency reed-marsh land tax was restored; now sand fields cannot bear such harassment.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover at the Xinsi military emergency reed-marsh land tax was restored; sand fields cannot bear such harassment now.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「誠如卿言。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Truly as you say."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Truly as you say."

sentences.zh: 」顒至中書，召俊彥切責之曰：「汝言利求進，萬一為國生事，斬汝不足以塞責。

translations.literal: Yong went to the Secretariat and summoned Junyan, sharply reproaching him: "You speak of profit seeking advancement — if by chance you cause trouble for the state, beheading you would not suffice to meet the blame."
translations.idiomatic: Yong went to the Secretariat and summoned Junyan, sharply reproaching him, "You speak of profit seeking advancement — if you cause trouble for the state, beheading you would not suffice to answer for it."

sentences.zh: 」俊彥皇恐汗下。

translations.literal: Junyan was terrified, sweat streaming down.
translations.idiomatic: Junyan was terrified, sweat streaming down his face.

sentences.zh: 是日，詔沙田、蘆場並罷。

translations.literal: That same day an edict abolished taxation on sand fields and reed marshes together.
translations.idiomatic: That same day an edict abolished taxation on sand fields and reed marshes.

sentences.zh: 御史林安宅請兩淮行鐵錢，顒力言不可，安宅不能平，既入樞府，乃上章攻顒云：「顒之子受宣州富人周良臣錢百萬，得監鎮江大軍倉。

translations.literal: Censor Lin Anzhai requested iron coinage in the two Huai circuits. Yong strongly argued against it; Anzhai could not accept this. Once he entered the Bureau of Military Affairs he submitted a memorial attacking Yong, saying: "Yong's son received a million cash from the wealthy man Zhou Liangchen of Xuan Prefecture and obtained supervision of the Jiang Army granary."
translations.idiomatic: Censor Lin Anzhai requested iron coinage in the two Huai circuits. Yong strongly opposed it, and Anzhai resented the opposition. Once in the Bureau of Military Affairs he submitted a memorial attacking Yong, claiming Yong's son had received a million cash from the wealthy Zhou Liangchen of Xuan Prefecture to obtain supervision of the Jiang Army granary.

sentences.zh: 」御史王伯庠亦論之。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Wang Boxiang also impeached him.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Wang Boxiang also impeached him.

sentences.zh: 顒乞下吏辯明，乃以資政殿學士提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Yong requested that the matter be sent to officials for clarification and was then appointed Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance and Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace.
translations.idiomatic: Yong requested a formal investigation and was appointed Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance and Commissioner of the Tongxiao Palace.

sentences.zh: 上下其事臨安府，時王炎知臨安，上令炎親鞫置對，無秋毫跡。

translations.literal: The matter was referred to Lin'an Prefecture; at the time Wang Yan was prefect of Lin'an, and the emperor ordered Yan personally to conduct interrogation and confrontation — not a trace was found.
translations.idiomatic: The matter was referred to Lin'an Prefecture; Wang Yan was then prefect, and the emperor ordered him to conduct the interrogation personally — not a trace of wrongdoing was found.

sentences.zh: 獄奏，上以安宅、伯庠風聞失實，並免所居官，仍貶安宅筠州，召顒赴闕。

translations.literal: When the case was reported, the emperor held that Anzhai and Boxiang had acted on rumor without basis and dismissed both from office, also demoting Anzhai to Yun Prefecture and summoning Yong to court.
translations.idiomatic: When the case was reported, the emperor ruled that Anzhai and Boxiang had acted on unfounded rumor and dismissed both from office, demoting Anzhai to Yun Prefecture and summoning Yong to court.

sentences.zh: 入見，上勞之曰：「卿之清德自是愈光矣。」

translations.literal: On audience the emperor comforted him, saying: "Your integrity is thereby all the brighter."
translations.idiomatic: On audience the emperor comforted him, saying, "Your integrity shines all the brighter for this."

sentences.zh: 除知樞密院事，未拜，進尚書左僕射兼樞密使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs but had not yet received the appointment when he was advanced to Left Grand Counsellor and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs; before the appointment ceremony he was advanced to Left Grand Counsellor and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 顒首薦汪應辰、王十朋、陳良翰、周操、陳之茂、芮曄、林光朝等，可備執政、侍從、臺諫，上嘉納。

translations.literal: Yong first recommended Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Chen Lianghan, Zhou Cao, Chen Zhimao, Rui Ye, Lin Guangchao, and others as fit for the government, attendant office, and censorial posts; the emperor praised and accepted this.
translations.idiomatic: Yong first recommended Wang Yingchen, Wang Shipeng, Chen Lianghan, Zhou Cao, Chen Zhimao, Rui Ye, Lin Guangchao, and others as fit for high office, attendant posts, and censorial roles; the emperor praised and accepted the recommendations.

sentences.zh: 又言：「自古明君用人，使賢使愚，使姦使盜，惟去泰甚。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since antiquity enlightened rulers in employing men have used the worthy and the foolish, the treacherous and the thieving — only removing the excessively bad."
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Since antiquity enlightened rulers have employed both the worthy and the foolish, the treacherous and the thieving — only removing the excessively bad."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「固然。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "So it is."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Indeed."

sentences.zh: 虞有禹、皐，亦有共、驩；

translations.literal: Yu had Yu and Gao, but also had Gong and Huan;
translations.idiomatic: Under Yu there were Yu and Gao, but also Gong and Huan;

sentences.zh: 周有旦、奭，亦有管、蔡，在用不用。

translations.literal: Zhou had Dan and Shi, but also had Guan and Cai — it lay in using or not using them.
translations.idiomatic: Under Zhou there were Dan and Shi, but also Guan and Cai — the difference lay in using them or not.

sentences.zh: 」顒曰：「誠如聖訓，但今日在朝雖未見有共、驩、管、蔡，然有竊弄威福者，臣不敢隱。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Truly as Your Majesty instructs, but though today at court one does not yet see Gong, Huan, Guan, or Cai, there are those who secretly manipulate power and favor; your subject dares not conceal this."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "Truly as Your Majesty instructs, but though one does not yet see Gong, Huan, Guan, or Cai at court today, there are those who secretly manipulate power and favor, and I dare not conceal it."

sentences.zh: 」上問為誰，顒以龍大淵對，語在《陳俊卿傳》。

translations.literal: The emperor asked who; Yong answered Long Dayuan — the account is in the biography of Chen Junqing.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked who; Yong named Long Dayuan — the account is in the biography of Chen Junqing.

sentences.zh: 上以國用未裕，詔宰相兼國用使，參政同知國用事，顒乃言：「今日費財養兵為甚，兵多則有冗卒虛籍，無事則費財，有事則不可用。

translations.literal: Because state revenues were not yet ample, an edict ordered the chief minister to concurrently serve as Commissioner of State Revenue and vice councillors to concurrently direct state revenue affairs. Yong then said: "Today the greatest expense is maintaining troops. When troops are many there are redundant soldiers and empty registers; in peace they waste funds, in war they cannot be used."
translations.idiomatic: Because state revenues were not yet ample, an edict ordered the chief minister to serve concurrently as Commissioner of State Revenue. Yong then said, "Today's greatest expense is maintaining troops. When troops are many there are redundant soldiers and empty registers; in peace they waste funds, in war they are useless."

sentences.zh: 雖曰汰之，旋即招之，欲足國用，當嚴於汰、緩於招可也。

translations.literal: Though it is said they are reduced, they are immediately recruited again; to fill state coffers, reduction should be strict and recruitment slow.
translations.idiomatic: Though troops are said to be reduced, they are immediately recruited again; to fill state coffers, reduction should be strict and recruitment slow.

sentences.zh: 孔子曰：『節用而愛人』。

translations.literal: Confucius said: 'Be economical in expenditure and love the people.'
translations.idiomatic: Confucius said, 'Be economical in expenditure and love the people.'

sentences.zh: 蓋節用，則愛人之政自行於其間，若欲生財，祗費民財爾。

translations.literal: For if expenditure is economized, then the policy of loving the people will naturally operate within it; if one wishes to generate wealth, one only wastes the people's wealth.
translations.idiomatic: If expenditure is economized, the policy of loving the people operates naturally; if one seeks to generate wealth, one only wastes the people's wealth.

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「此至言也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "These are supreme words."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "These are supreme words."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「建康劉源嘗賂近習，朕欲遣王抃廉其姦。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Liu Yuan of Jiankang once bribed close attendants; I wish to send Wang Bian to investigate his wickedness."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Liu Yuan of Jiankang once bribed close attendants; I wish to send Wang Bian to investigate his corruption."

sentences.zh: 」顒曰：「臣恐廉者甚於姦者。

translations.literal: Yong said: "Your subject fears the investigator may prove worse than the corrupt man."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "I fear the investigator may prove worse than the corrupt man."

sentences.zh: 」乃止。

translations.literal: The plan was then stopped.
translations.idiomatic: The plan was then abandoned.

sentences.zh: 乾道三年冬至，上親郊而雷，顒引漢故事上印綬，提舉太平興國宮。

translations.literal: At the winter solstice of the third year of Qiandao the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice and thunder struck. Yong cited Han precedent and submitted his seal and cord, and was appointed Commissioner of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the winter solstice of the third year of Qiandao the emperor personally performed the suburban sacrifice and thunder struck. Yong cited Han precedent and submitted his seal and cord, and was appointed Commissioner of the Taiping Xingguo Palace.

sentences.zh: 歸至家，不疾而薨，年六十八。

translations.literal: Returning home he died without illness, aged sixty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: Returning home he died without prior illness, aged sixty-eight.

sentences.zh: 以觀文殿學士致仕，贈特進，諡「正簡」。

translations.literal: Having retired as Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, he was posthumously appointed Special Advance and given the posthumous title Zhengjian.
translations.idiomatic: Having retired as Grand Academician of the Hall for Observing Culture, he was posthumously appointed Special Advance and given the posthumous title Zhengjian.

sentences.zh: 顒為人簡易清介，與物若無忤，至處大事毅然不可奪。

translations.literal: Yong as a man was simple, upright, and pure; with others he seemed never to give offense, yet when facing great affairs he was resolute and could not be swayed.
translations.idiomatic: Yong was simple, upright, and pure; with others he seemed never to give offense, yet in great affairs he was resolute and could not be swayed.

sentences.zh: 友人高登嘗上書譏切時相，名捕甚急。

translations.literal: His friend Gao Deng once submitted a memorial sharply criticizing the chief minister and was urgently sought by name.
translations.idiomatic: His friend Gao Deng once submitted a memorial sharply criticizing the chief minister and was urgently sought by name.

sentences.zh: 顒與同邸，擿令逸去，登曰：「不為君累乎？

translations.literal: Yong lodged in the same residence and urged him to flee. Deng said: "Will this not implicate you?"
translations.idiomatic: Yong lodged in the same residence and urged him to flee. Deng said, "Will this not implicate you?"

sentences.zh: 」顒曰：「以獲罪，固所願也。

translations.literal: Yong said: "To incur guilt for this is exactly what I wish."
translations.idiomatic: Yong said, "To incur guilt for this is exactly what I wish."

sentences.zh: 」即為具舟，舟移乃去。

translations.literal: He immediately prepared a boat for him; only when the boat moved off did he leave.
translations.idiomatic: He immediately prepared a boat for him and left only after the boat had departed.

sentences.zh: 自初仕至宰相，服食、僮妾、田宅不改其舊。

translations.literal: From first taking office to reaching the chancellorship, his food, clothing, servants, concubines, fields, and houses did not change from what they had been.
translations.idiomatic: From first taking office to reaching the chancellorship, his food, clothing, servants, concubines, fields, and houses remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 葉衡，字夢錫，婺州金華人。

translations.literal: Ye Heng, styled Mengxi, was a native of Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Heng, courtesy name Mengxi, was a native of Jinhua in Wu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 紹興十八年進士第，調福州寧德簿，攝尉。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the eighteenth year of Shaoxing, was assigned as Clerk of Ningde in Fuzhou, and administered as assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1148, was assigned as Clerk of Ningde in Fuzhou, and administered as assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 以獲鹽寇改秩，知臨安府於潛縣。

translations.literal: For capturing salt smugglers he was promoted in rank and served as magistrate of Yuqian County in Lin'an Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: For capturing salt smugglers he was promoted in rank and served as magistrate of Yuqian County in Lin'an Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 戶版積弊，富民多隱漏，貧弱困於倍輸，衡定為九等，自五以下除其籍，而均其額於上之四等，貧者頓蘇。

translations.literal: Household registers had long been corrupt; wealthy families often concealed and evaded registration while the poor and weak suffered from doubled levies. Heng fixed nine grades; from the fifth grade down registers were removed and their quotas distributed among the upper four grades, and the poor were suddenly relieved.
translations.idiomatic: Household registers had long been corrupt; wealthy families concealed registration while the poor suffered doubled levies. Heng fixed nine grades; from the fifth grade down registers were removed and quotas distributed among the upper four grades, and the poor were suddenly relieved.

sentences.zh: 征科為期限榜縣門，俾里正諭民，不遣一吏而賦自足。

translations.literal: For tax collection he posted deadlines at the county gate and had village heads instruct the people, without sending a single clerk yet the levies were fully collected.
translations.idiomatic: For tax collection he posted deadlines at the county gate and had village heads instruct the people, without sending a single clerk yet levies were fully collected.

sentences.zh: 歲災，蝗不入境。

translations.literal: In a drought year locusts did not enter the district.
translations.idiomatic: In a drought year locusts did not enter the district.

sentences.zh: 治為諸邑最。

translations.literal: His governance ranked first among all districts.
translations.idiomatic: His governance ranked first among all districts.

sentences.zh: 郡以政績聞，即召對，上曰：「聞卿作縣有法。

translations.literal: The prefecture reported his governing achievements and he was summoned for audience. The emperor said: "I hear that in governing your county you had method."
translations.idiomatic: The prefecture reported his achievements and he was summoned for audience. The emperor said, "I hear you governed your county with method."

sentences.zh: 」遣還任。

translations.literal: He was sent back to his post.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent back to his post.

sentences.zh: 擢知常州。

translations.literal: He was promoted to serve as prefect of Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to serve as prefect of Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 時水潦為災，衡發倉為糜以食饑者。

translations.literal: At the time flooding caused disaster; Heng opened the granaries and made gruel to feed the hungry.
translations.idiomatic: At the time flooding caused disaster; Heng opened the granaries and made gruel to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 或言常平不可輕發，衡曰：「儲蓄正備緩急，可視民饑而不救耶？

translations.literal: Some said the ever-normal granaries should not be lightly opened. Heng said: "Stores exist precisely for emergencies — can one watch the people starve and not save them?"
translations.idiomatic: Some said the ever-normal granaries should not be lightly opened. Heng said, "Stores exist for emergencies — can one watch the people starve and not save them?"

sentences.zh: 」疫大作，衡單騎命醫藥自隨，偏問疾苦，活者甚眾。

translations.literal: When plague broke out severely, Heng rode alone with medicines at his side, going everywhere to ask after suffering; very many were saved.
translations.idiomatic: When plague broke out severely, Heng rode alone with medicines at his side, going everywhere to ask after the afflicted; very many were saved.

sentences.zh: 檄晉陵丞李孟堅攝無錫縣，有政聲，衡薦於上，即除知秀州。

translations.literal: He ordered Jinling Assistant Magistrate Li Mengjian to administer Wuxi County; Mengjian had a good governing reputation and Heng recommended him to the throne; he was immediately appointed prefect of Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered Jinling Assistant Magistrate Li Mengjian to administer Wuxi County; Mengjian had a good governing reputation and Heng recommended him; he was immediately appointed prefect of Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 上之信其言如此。

translations.literal: Such was the emperor's trust in his words.
translations.idiomatic: Such was the emperor's trust in his judgment.

sentences.zh: 除太府少卿。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Director of the Palace Storehouse.

sentences.zh: 合肥瀕湖有圩田四十里，衡奏：「募民以耕，歲可得穀數十萬，蠲租稅，二三年後阡陌成，仿營田，官私各收其半。

translations.literal: By Lake Chao in Hefei there were forty li of polder fields. Heng memorialized: "Recruit people to cultivate them and each year several hundred thousand bushels of grain can be obtained. Exempt rent and tax; after two or three years when paths and fields are formed, model this on garrison fields and let official and private each receive half."
translations.idiomatic: By Lake Chao in Hefei there were forty li of polder fields. Heng memorialized, "Recruit people to cultivate them and each year several hundred thousand bushels can be obtained. Exempt rent and tax; after two or three years, model this on garrison fields and let official and private each receive half."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was accepted.

sentences.zh: 除戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 時鹽課大虧，衡奏：「年來課入不增，私販害之也，宜自煮鹽之地為之制，司火之起伏，稽灶之多寡，亭戶本錢以時給之，鹽之委積以時收之，擇廉能吏察之，私販自絕矣。

translations.literal: At the time salt revenue was greatly depleted. Heng memorialized: "In recent years revenue has not increased because private trafficking harms it. Regulations should be made from the salt-boiling regions themselves, controlling the rise and fall of fires, checking the number of furnaces, paying stove households their capital on schedule, collecting accumulated salt on schedule, and assigning incorrupt and capable officials to inspect — private trafficking will cease of itself."
translations.idiomatic: At the time salt revenue was greatly depleted. Heng memorialized, "Revenue has not increased because private trafficking harms it. Regulations should be made from the salt-boiling regions, controlling fires, checking furnaces, paying stove households on schedule, collecting accumulated salt on schedule, and assigning incorrupt officials to inspect — private trafficking will cease."

sentences.zh: 」仍命措置官三人：淮南於通州，浙東於明州，浙西於秀州。

translations.literal: Three arrangement officials were also appointed: for Huainan at Tongzhou, for eastern Zhe at Mingzhou, and for western Zhe at Xiuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Three arrangement officials were appointed: for Huainan at Tongzhou, for eastern Zhe at Mingzhou, and for western Zhe at Xiuzhou.

sentences.zh: 丁母憂。

translations.literal: He entered mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: He entered mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 起復，知盧州，未行，除樞密都承旨。

translations.literal: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed prefect of Luzhou but had not yet departed when he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled from mourning, he was appointed prefect of Luzhou but had not yet departed when he was appointed Chief Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 奏馬政之弊，宜命統制一員各領馬若干匹，歲終計其數為殿最。

translations.literal: He memorialized on abuses in horse administration and proposed that one controller be assigned to each group of horses, with annual counts determining merit and demerit.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on abuses in horse administration and proposed that one controller be assigned to each group of horses, with annual counts determining merit and demerit.

sentences.zh: 李垕應賢良方正對策，近訐直，入第四等，衡奏：「陛下赦其狂而取其忠，足以顯容諫之盛。

translations.literal: Li Yao answered the examination for Worthy and Upright and Plainspoken; his responses were nearly too blunt and he ranked in the fourth grade. Heng memorialized: "Your Majesty pardons his rashness and takes his loyalty — this is enough to display the greatness of tolerating remonstrance."
translations.idiomatic: Li Yao answered the examination for Worthy and Upright and Plainspoken; his responses were nearly too blunt and he ranked in the fourth grade. Heng memorialized, "Your Majesty pardons his rashness and takes his loyalty — this is enough to display the greatness of tolerating remonstrance."

sentences.zh: 」乃賜垕制科出身。

translations.literal: Yao was then granted status as a decree examination graduate.
translations.idiomatic: Yao was then granted status as a decree examination graduate.

sentences.zh: 有言江、淮兵籍偽濫，詔衡按視，賜以袍帶、鞍馬、弓矢，且命衡措置民兵，咸稱得治兵之要。

translations.literal: Some reported that Jiang and Huai military registers were fraudulent and inflated. An edict ordered Heng to inspect; he was granted robe, belt, saddle, horse, bow, and arrows, and also ordered to arrange militia — all praised that he had grasped the essentials of governing troops.
translations.idiomatic: Some reported that Jiang and Huai military registers were fraudulent. An edict ordered Heng to inspect; he was granted robe, belt, saddle, horse, bow, and arrows, and ordered to arrange militia — all praised that he had grasped the essentials of governing troops.

sentences.zh: 訖事赴闕，上御便殿閱武士，召衡預觀，賜酒，灑宸翰賜之。

translations.literal: When the task was completed he came to court; the emperor reviewed martial officers in the side hall and summoned Heng to observe, bestowing wine and sprinkling an imperial inscription as gift.
translations.idiomatic: When the task was completed he came to court; the emperor reviewed martial officers in the side hall and summoned Heng to observe, bestowing wine and an imperial inscription.

sentences.zh: 知荊南、成都、建康府，除戶部尚書，除簽書樞密院事，拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He served as prefect of Jingnan, Chengdu, and Jiankang, was appointed Minister of Revenue, Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as prefect of Jingnan, Chengdu, and Jiankang, was appointed Minister of Revenue, Signing Secretary of the Bureau of Military Affairs, and Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 衡奏二事：一，牧守將帥必擇材以稱其職，必久任以盡其材；

translations.literal: Heng memorialized on two matters: first, prefects, commanders, and generals must be chosen for ability to fit their posts and must serve long terms to exhaust their talent;
translations.idiomatic: Heng memorialized on two matters: first, prefects, commanders, and generals must be chosen for ability and must serve long terms to exhaust their talent;

sentences.zh: 二，令戶部取湖廣會子實數，盡以京會立限易之。

translations.literal: second, order the Ministry of Revenue to take the actual numbers of Hu-Guang treasury notes and within a fixed term exchange them all for capital notes.
translations.idiomatic: second, order the Ministry of Revenue to take the actual numbers of Hu-Guang treasury notes and within a fixed term exchange them all for capital notes.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was accepted.
translations.idiomatic: This was accepted.

sentences.zh: 拜右丞相兼樞密使。

translations.literal: He was appointed Right Grand Chancellor and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Right Grand Chancellor and Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 上銳意恢復，凡將帥、器械、山川、防守悉經思慮，奏對畢，從容賜坐，講論機密，或不時召對。

translations.literal: The emperor was keen on recovery; generals, weapons, mountains and rivers, and defenses were all carefully considered. When memorial audiences were finished he would grant him a seat at leisure to discuss secrets, or sometimes summon him at irregular hours.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was keen on recovery; generals, weapons, terrain, and defenses were all carefully considered. After memorial audiences he would grant him a seat to discuss secrets, or sometimes summon him at irregular hours.

sentences.zh: 時會子浸患折閱，手詔賜衡曰：「會子雖曰流通，終未盡愜人意，目即流使有二千二百餘萬。

translations.literal: At the time treasury notes were increasingly troubled by depreciation. A handwritten edict was bestowed on Heng, saying: "Though treasury notes are said to circulate, they still do not fully satisfy people's wishes; currently more than twenty-two million are in circulation."
translations.idiomatic: At the time treasury notes were increasingly troubled by depreciation. A handwritten edict was bestowed on Heng, saying, "Though treasury notes are said to circulate, they still do not fully satisfy; currently more than twenty-two million are in circulation."

sentences.zh: 今用上下庫黃金、白金、銅錢九百萬，內藏庫五百萬，並蜀中錢物七百萬，盡易會子之數，專命卿措置，日近而辦，卿真宰相才也。」

translations.literal: Now use nine million in gold, silver, and copper cash from the upper and lower treasuries, five million from the inner storehouse, and seven million in goods and cash from Shu — altogether to replace the full number of notes. You alone are charged with arrangement; it will be done soon — you are truly chancellor material."
translations.idiomatic: Now use nine million in gold, silver, and copper cash from the upper and lower treasuries, five million from the inner storehouse, and seven million from Shu — altogether to replace the full number of notes. You alone are charged with this — you are truly chancellor material."

sentences.zh: 一日，上曲宴宰執於凝碧，上曰：「自三代而下，至於漢、唐，治日常少，亂日常多，何也？

translations.literal: One day the emperor gave an informal banquet to the chief ministers at Ningbi and said: "From the Three Dynasties down through Han and Tang, days of order were always fewer and days of disorder always more — why?"
translations.idiomatic: One day the emperor gave an informal banquet to the chief ministers at Ningbi and said, "From the Three Dynasties down through Han and Tang, days of order were always fewer and days of disorder always more — why?"

sentences.zh: 」衡奏：「聖君不常有，周八百年，稱極治成、康而已。

translations.literal: Heng memorialized: "Sagely rulers are not constant; in eight hundred years of Zhou, only the utmost order of Cheng and Kang is praised."
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "Sagely rulers are not constant; in eight hundred years of Zhou, only the utmost order of Cheng and Kang is praised."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕觀《無逸篇》，見周公為成王歷言商、周之君享國長遠，真萬世龜鑑。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When I read the 'Against Idleness' chapter, I see the Duke of Zhou for King Cheng repeatedly speaking of Shang and Zhou rulers who enjoyed long reigns — it is truly a mirror for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When I read the 'Against Idleness' chapter, I see the Duke of Zhou for King Cheng repeatedly speaking of Shang and Zhou rulers who enjoyed long reigns — it is truly a mirror for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 」衡奏：「願陛下常以《無逸》為龜鑑，社稷之福。

translations.literal: Heng memorialized: "I hope Your Majesty will always take the 'Against Idleness' as a mirror — this is the fortune of the altars of state."
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "I hope Your Majesty will always take the 'Against Idleness' as a mirror — this is the fortune of the realm."

sentences.zh: 」上又言：「朝廷所用，正論其人如何，不可有黨。

translations.literal: The emperor also said: "In employing men at court, one should simply judge the man — there must be no factions."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "In employing men at court, one should judge the man — there must be no factions."

sentences.zh: 如唐牛、李之黨，相攻四十年，緣主聽不明至此。

translations.literal: Like the Niu-Li factions of Tang, attacking each other for forty years — it came to this because the ruler's hearing was not clear.
translations.idiomatic: Like the Niu-Li factions of Tang, attacking each other for forty years — it came to this because the ruler's hearing was not clear.

sentences.zh: 文宗曰：『去河北賊易，去朝中朋黨難』。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong said: 'Removing the bandits north of the Yellow River is easy; removing factional cliques at court is hard.'
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong said, 'Removing the bandits north of the Yellow River is easy; removing factional cliques at court is hard.'

sentences.zh: 朕嘗笑之。

translations.literal: I once laughed at this.
translations.idiomatic: I once laughed at this.

sentences.zh: 」衡奏：「文宗優遊不斷，故有此語。

translations.literal: Heng memorialized: "Wenzong was leisurely and indecisive, hence these words."
translations.idiomatic: Heng replied, "Wenzong was leisurely and indecisive, hence these words."

sentences.zh: 陛下英明聖武，誠非難事。」

translations.literal: Your Majesty is bright, sage, and martial — truly this is no difficult matter."
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty is bright, sage, and martial — truly this is no difficult matter."

sentences.zh: 御寶實封令與臨安府竇思永改合入官，衡奏：「選人改官，非奏對稱旨，則用考舉磨勘，一旦特旨與之，非陛下愛惜人才之意。

translations.literal: An imperial sealed order directed that Dou Siyong of Lin'an Prefecture be given a promotion to the appropriate office. Heng memorialized: "For a selection official to change rank, unless he is commended at a memorial audience, the regular path is examination and merit review — to give a special order at once is not Your Majesty's intent to cherish talent."
translations.idiomatic: An imperial sealed order directed that Dou Siyong of Lin'an Prefecture be given a promotion. Heng memorialized, "For a selection official to change rank, unless commended at audience, the regular path is examination and merit review — a special order at once is not Your Majesty's intent to cherish talent."

sentences.zh: 」上亟收前命。

translations.literal: The emperor immediately withdrew the previous order.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor immediately withdrew the order.

sentences.zh: 上諭執政，選使求河南，衡奏：「司諫湯邦彥有口辨，宜使金。

translations.literal: The emperor instructed the chief ministers to select an envoy to seek Henan. Heng memorialized: "Remonstrance Official Tang Bangyan has a glib tongue and should be sent to Jin."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor instructed the chief ministers to select an envoy to seek Henan. Heng memorialized, "Remonstrance Official Tang Bangyan has a glib tongue and should be sent to Jin."

sentences.zh: 」邦彥請對，問所以遣，既知薦出於衡，恨衡擠己，聞衡對客有訕上語，奏之，上大怒。

translations.literal: Bangyan requested audience and asked why he was being sent; once he learned the recommendation came from Heng he resented Heng for pushing him aside. Hearing that Heng had mockingly spoken of the emperor before guests, he reported this and the emperor was greatly angered.
translations.idiomatic: Bangyan requested audience and asked why he was being sent; learning the recommendation came from Heng he resented Heng for pushing him aside. Hearing that Heng had mockingly spoken of the emperor before guests, he reported this and the emperor was greatly angered.

sentences.zh: 即日罷相，責授安德軍節度副使，郴州安置。

translations.literal: That same day Heng was dismissed as chancellor, demoted to Military Vice Commissioner of Ande, and ordered to reside in Chen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: That same day Heng was dismissed as chancellor, demoted to Military Vice Commissioner of Ande, and ordered to reside in Chen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 邦彥使還，果辱命，上震怒，竄之嶺南，詔衡自便，復官與祠。

translations.literal: When Bangyan returned from his mission he indeed disgraced it; the emperor was shaken with anger and exiled him to Lingnan. An edict restored Heng to free movement and reinstated his rank and sinecure.
translations.idiomatic: When Bangyan returned from his mission he indeed disgraced it; the emperor was shaken with anger and exiled him to Lingnan. An edict restored Heng to free movement and reinstated his rank and sinecure.

sentences.zh: 年六十有二薨，贈資政殿學士。

translations.literal: He died aged sixty-two and was posthumously appointed Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance.
translations.idiomatic: He died aged sixty-two and was posthumously appointed Academician of the Hall for Assistance in Governance.

sentences.zh: 衡負才足智，理兵事甚悉，由小官不十年至宰相，進用之驟，人謂出於曾覿云。

translations.literal: Heng was talented and resourceful, understood military affairs thoroughly, and from a minor post reached the chancellorship in less than ten years. The speed of his advancement — people said it came through Zeng Di.
translations.idiomatic: Heng was talented and resourceful, understood military affairs thoroughly, and from a minor post reached the chancellorship in less than ten years. People said his rapid advancement came through Zeng Di.

sentences.zh: 論曰：陳康伯以經濟自任，臨事明斷。

translations.literal: The commentators say: Chen Kangbo took statecraft upon himself and was clear and decisive in affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The commentators say: Chen Kangbo took statecraft upon himself and was clear and decisive in affairs.

sentences.zh: 梁克家才優識遠，謀國盡忠。

translations.literal: Liang Kejia was talented with far-reaching judgment and served the state with full loyalty.
translations.idiomatic: Liang Kejia was talented with far-reaching judgment and served the state with full loyalty.

sentences.zh: 至若汪澈之論事忠愨，薦達人才，葉義問直言正色，掃除秦檜餘黨，然不長於兵，臨敵失措，豈優議論而劣事功者歟？

translations.literal: As for Wang Che's loyal and earnest policy debate and recommendation of talent, and Ye Yiwen's frank speech and upright bearing in sweeping away Qin Hui's remaining partisans — yet not being skilled in military affairs and losing composure before the enemy — were they superior in debate but inferior in practical achievement?
translations.idiomatic: As for Wang Che's loyal policy debate and recommendation of talent, and Ye Yiwen's frank speech in sweeping away Qin Hui's remaining partisans — yet not being skilled in military affairs and losing composure before the enemy — were they superior in debate but inferior in practical achievement?

sentences.zh: 葉顒清儉正直，而衡才智有餘，蓋亦一時之選云。

translations.literal: Ye Yong was frugal, upright, and honest, while Heng had talent and wisdom in abundance — all were choices of their time.
translations.idiomatic: Ye Yong was frugal, upright, and honest, while Heng had talent and wisdom in abundance — all were choices of their time.
